definition_zh: 不负责任的；不承担责任的；缺乏责任感的；不可靠的
definition_en: not showing proper care for what one is expected to take care of
core_image: 把该关的闸门只关了一半，然后转身走开
scene: 他把公共自行车随手扔在车道上就走，害得后面的人差点撞上，路人摇头说他太不负责了。He left the shared bike in the middle of the lane and walked away, which his neighbours called irresponsible.
sceneCN: 这里 irresponsible 是「不负责任的」（第 1 个义项：对应当照料的事情缺乏应有担当）；句意：他把共享单车丢在车道中间就走，邻居们都觉得这很不负责。

pos.zh: 不负责任的；不承担责任的；不可靠的

derivatives.zh: 不负责任；责任感缺失
不负责任地
负责的；有责任的
责任；职责

senses.title: Not taking proper care
senses.titleCN: 不负责任的；缺乏责任感的
senses.definition: failing to take proper care of what one is supposed to look after
senses.definitionCN: 对本应照料的事情没有给予应有的关心
senses.example: Leaving a child alone at home all day is irresponsible.
senses.exampleCN: 把孩子一个人整天留在家里是不负责任的。
senses.why: Responsible is built on response, a promising back an answer for something, and in- cancels that promise, so the word names someone who does not answer for any duty.
senses.whyCN: responsible 建立在 response（应答）之上，意为对某事给出回应、担起责任；in- 否定这一承诺，所以这个词指的是不肯为职责作出交代的人。

senses.title: Not accountable before the law
senses.titleCN: 法律上不负责任的；不承担责任的
senses.definition: not holding a formal duty that can be enforced in a court
senses.definitionCN: 不承担可在法庭上追究的正式义务
senses.example: Under the contract, the supplier is irresponsible for losses caused by storms.
senses.exampleCN: 根据合同，供应商对暴风雨造成的损失不承担责任。
senses.why: In legal use, responsibility drops away; only the absence of liability remains, so the word becomes a formal way of saying not liable.
senses.whyCN: 在法律用法中，「职责」这一含义被剥离，只剩「不承担」，于是变成正式场合下表示「不负责任」的说法。

senses.title: Careless in an unthinking way
senses.definition: acting without thinking about the results for oneself or others
senses.definitionCN: 行动时不顾自己或他人后果
senses.example: It was irresponsible to lend the car to a new driver for a midnight race.
senses.exampleCN: 把车借给新手司机去午夜飙车，是不计后果的做法。
senses.why: The sense widens from duty to consequences: a person who ignores the results of an act is seen as careless in a reckless way.
senses.whyCN: 该义从「职责」扩展到「后果」：无视行为后果的人，就被看作十足的鲁莽马虎。

senses.title: Not reliable for a job or matter
senses.definition: not reliable enough to be trusted with important work
senses.definitionCN: 可靠程度不足以被托付重要工作
senses.example: The team removed an irresponsible member from the planning group.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把一名不可靠的成员移出了筹备组。
senses.why: Once a person does not answer for duties, others stop giving them duties, so the word settles into a description of someone who cannot be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 一个人既不为职责作交代，别人也就不再托付职责，于是这个词沉淀为「托付不了事」的描述。

intro.en: Irresponsible joins the negative in- to responsible, which comes from Latin respondere, to answer; the English adjective is first recorded in the later seventeenth century.
intro.cn: irresponsible 由否定前缀 in- 与 responsible 组成；responsible 源自拉丁语 respondere（作答）；英语形容词形式在十七世纪后期才见于记录。

items.en: Respondere is re- plus spondere, to promise, and means to promise back or answer.
items.cn: respondere 是 re- 加 spondere（承诺），意为许诺回去、作出答复。

items.en: The medieval form responsible names a person who owes an answer before a court or landlord.
items.cn: 中古法语中表示作答的 responsible 形式，指在法庭或地主面前负有答复义务的人。

items.en: Responsible enters English with the legal sense of answerable.
items.cn: responsible 带着法律上「需应答、受追究」的意义进入英语。

items.en: The negative in- yields irresponsible, recorded from the later seventeenth century.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 造出 irresponsible，其记录可追溯至十七世纪后期。

items.en: In modern use the word spreads from law to family, finance, and personal conduct.
items.cn: 现代用法中，这个词从法律领域扩展到家庭、财务与个人行为。

items.en: In the twenty-first century it is a standard word in education, journalism, and public policy.
items.cn: 进入二十一世纪，它已是教育、新闻与公共政策中的常用词。

note.en: Irresponsible negates responsible; the look-alike group covers the respons- family, and the near group covers words for careless conduct.
note.cn: irresponsible 是 responsible 的否定；形近组覆盖 respons- 词族，近义组覆盖表示马虎行为的词。

entries.definition: having a duty for something and answering for it
entries.definitionCN: 对某事负有职责的（去掉否定前缀后的原词）

entries.definition: a duty that one must answer for
quick to react in a positive way
entries.definitionCN: 反应积极的（同出 respond，但词尾不同）

entries.definition: not giving enough attention to what one is doing
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的；不留意的（侧重注意力不足，不一定涉及义务）

entries.definition: acting without thinking about danger or results
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽的；不计后果的（侧重危险）

entries.definition: not able to be trusted to do what is expected

normalIntro.en: Irresponsible is responsible with a leading in-, and responsible is built on response, the act of answering for something.
normalIntro.cn: irresponsible 就是给 responsible 加了个在前面的 in-，而 responsible 建立在 response（作答）之上。

normal.en: The base is response, so responsible means ready to answer for what one does.
normal.cn: 基础词是 response，所以 responsible 意为「肯为自己的行为作答」。

normal.en: The prefix in- before r becomes ir-, as in irregular and irrelevant.
normal.cn: in- 接在 r 前写作 ir-，如 irregular 与 irrelevant。

normal.en: The frame is be responsible for something, so the negative is irresponsible for that matter.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 be responsible for，否定形式则是对该事「不负责任」。

normal.en: The noun irresponsibility and the adverb irresponsibly follow the same pattern.
normal.cn: 名词 irresponsibility 与副词 irresponsibly 遵循同样的构词方式。

normal.en: The word appears often with behaviour, parents, and spending, which are all about duty.
normal.cn: 这个词常与行为、家长、开支这类都关乎职责的词搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a gate left half open with a promise still written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只关上了一半的闸门，上面还贴着写好的承诺。

abstract.en: Picture a contract with the duty line crossed out but the signature intact.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同，责任那一行被划掉，签名却还留着。

abstract.en: Picture a driver racing off while the car door hangs open behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车扬长而去，身后的车门还敞开着。

examples.en: It is irresponsible to spend money you do not really have.
examples.cn: 花自己其实没有的钱是不负责任的。

examples.en: The newspaper called the leak of private data irresponsible.
examples.cn: 报纸称泄露私人数据的行为是不负责任的。

examples.en: His irresponsible remark upset the whole team.
examples.cn: 他那句不负责任的话让整个团队都很不满。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唉，response 不了」——出了事「唉，没法 response（回应）」的人，就是不负责任。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ spondere（许诺）→ respondere（回答；应答）→ response（答复）+ -ible（能够……的）→ responsible（能作答的、负责任的）→ 加否定前缀 in-（在 r 前变 ir-）→ irresponsible，核心义「不肯作答」。

sensesIntro.en: Irresponsible begins with failing to care for what one should look after, then loses liability in law, widens to careless conduct, and ends as a label for someone unreliable.
sensesIntro.cn: irresponsible 先指不尽照料之责，再在法律中只剩「不承担责任」之意，继而扩展到马虎轻率的行为，最后成为形容「靠不住」的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate left half open by someone who walks away.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人把闸门只关了一半就转身走开。

branches.en: Failing a duty of care is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 不尽照料之责，是日常义项。

branches.en: In law the word names the absence of liability.
branches.cn: 在法律中，这个词指「不承担责任」。

branches.en: Careless behaviour is the sense about consequences.
branches.cn: 马虎鲁莽的行为，是关乎后果的义项。

branches.en: A person who does not answer for duties soon cannot be trusted with them.
branches.cn: 不为职责作答的人，很快就难以被托付职责。

branches.en: No legal liability and no thought of results both leave others to pay the cost.
branches.cn: 法律上不担责与不顾后果，最后都让别人来承担代价。

intro.en: Irresponsible puts the negative prefix in- on responsible, which is a Latin answer-word plus the adjective suffix -ible.
intro.cn: irresponsible 是在 responsible 前加否定前缀 in-，而 responsible 是一个拉丁语「作答」词加形容词后缀 -ible。

latinIntro.en: Latin respondere, from re- and spondere, means to promise back and answer; responsum gives the noun response.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 respondere 由 re- 与 spondere 组成，意为许诺回去、作出回答；名词 responsum 给出 response。

items.example: In- negates responsible.
items.exampleCN: in- 使 responsible 变为否定。

items.meaningCN: 不（接在 r 前时的拼写变体）
items.example: Ir- appears before the r of responsible.
items.exampleCN: ir- 出现在 responsible 的 r 之前。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of giving something back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「回过来」的意味。

items.example: Spondere supplies the promise inside the word.
items.exampleCN: spondere 提供词中的「承诺」含义。

items.example: Respondere is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: respondere 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: Response is the noun at the centre.
items.exampleCN: response 是这个词的核心名词。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms responsible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 构成 responsible。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms responsibility.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 responsibility。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms irresponsibly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 irresponsibly。

definition_zh: 不可撤销的；不可撤回的；不可改变的
definition_en: formally decided and impossible to cancel, withdraw, or change
core_image: 一枚已经盖下的印章：墨迹干透，再也收不回来
scene: 两位合伙人在合同末尾签了字。When the partners signed the contract, they made an irrevocable promise to share all future profits.
sceneCN: 这里 irrevocable 是「不能撤回的」（第 1 个义项：正式决定后无法取消）；句意：合伙人们签下合同时，做出了共享未来所有利润的不可撤销承诺。

pos.zh: 不可撤销的；不可撤回的

derivatives.zh: 不可撤销地；无可挽回地，由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成
撤销；撤回；废除，是这个词去掉否定前缀后的正面动词
可撤销的；可撤回的，是加上否定前缀 in- 之前的原形

senses.title: Impossible to withdraw formally
senses.definition: officially agreed and impossible to cancel or take back
senses.definitionCN: 已正式同意，无法取消或收回
senses.example: Once signed, the contract is irrevocable.
senses.exampleCN: 协议一经签署便不可撤销。
senses.why: The prefix ir- turns revocable into its opposite: what cannot be called back again.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 ir- 把 revocable 变成反义，表示无法再次「召回、收回」，所以是不可撤销的。

senses.title: Beyond undoing
senses.titleCN: 无法挽回的；不可改变的
senses.definition: so settled that nothing can undo it or reverse its results
senses.definitionCN: 已经确定下来，任何事物都无法消除或逆转其结果
senses.example: Their quarrel had an irrevocable effect on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的争吵对团队造成了无法挽回的影响。
senses.why: The image of a dried seal carries over to results that can no longer be taken back.
senses.whyCN: 干透的印章意象延伸到结果上：事情一旦造成，同样收回不了，就成了无法挽回的。

senses.title: Final and binding
senses.definition: a decision already final, which the person who made it cannot change
senses.definitionCN: 已经最终确定、做出者也无法更改的决定
senses.example: The court ruling was irrevocable, so no appeal was possible.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的裁决是终局的，因此无法上诉。
senses.why: A final legal decision is treated like a stamp that cannot be lifted off the page.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的终局裁决就像一枚揭不下来的印章：已经定案，自己也不能再改。

intro.en: Irrevocable comes from Latin in- not plus revocare to call back, which gives Latin irrevocabilis.
intro.cn: irrevocable 来自拉丁语前缀 in-（不）加 revocare（召回），合为拉丁语 irrevocabilis。

items.en: Vocare means to call, and the prefix re- means back, giving revocare.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤，前缀 re- 意为往回，合起来是 revocare。

items.en: The prefix in- negates the verb, and irrevocabilis means cannot be called back.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 使动词变成否定，irrevocabilis 意为不能被召回。

items.en: Late Latin legal writers pair the word with wills and oaths.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的法律文本把这个词与遗嘱、誓言配在一起。

items.en: The form passes through French as irrévocable.
items.cn: 这个词经由法语 irrévocable 过渡。

items.en: English uses the word for contracts, verdicts, and deep regret.
items.cn: 近代英语用它描述合同、裁决与深深的遗憾。

note.en: Irrevocable belongs to the family of revoke, revocable, and vocare, and it stands beside words for final or permanent.
note.cn: irrevocable 属于 revoke、revocable 与 vocare 这一词族，并与表示「最终、永久」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to cancel a decision or promise officially
able to be cancelled
in a way that cannot be undone
showing no respect
entries.definitionCN: 不敬的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: last and not changeable
lasting and not expected to change
that must be obeyed by law

normalIntro.en: Irrevocable is revocable with a negative ir- in front: nothing can call the decision back.
normalIntro.cn: irrevocable 就是 revocable 加否定前缀 ir-：决定再也叫不回来了。

normal.en: Revoke means to call an order back, and ir- denies that possibility.
normal.cn: revoke 意为把命令叫回来，ir- 则否定了这种可能。

normal.en: The root voc- appears in voice, vocal, and vocation, all about calling.
normal.cn: 词根 voc- 见于 voice、vocal、vocation，都与「呼唤」有关。

normal.en: An irrevocable letter of credit is a bank promise that cannot be cancelled.
normal.cn: irrevocable letter of credit 是银行无法取消的付款承诺。

normal.en: Use the adverb irrevocably for results that cannot be undone.
normal.cn: 表示无法挽回的结果时用副词 irrevocably。

normal.en: Compare revocable: a revocable permit can still be cancelled,but an irrevocable one cannot.
normal.cn: 对比 revocable：可撤销的许可还能取消，不可撤销的就不能。

abstract.en: See a wax seal pressed hard onto paper, cooling into a shape that will not lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚火漆印重重盖在纸上，冷却成型后再也揭不下来。

abstract.en: Hear a shout fading away with no echo returning: the call back cannot happen.
abstract.cn: 想象一声呼喊消散，没有任何回声返回：叫回来的动作无法发生。

abstract.en: Picture a written verdict nailed to a wooden door, sealed for good.
abstract.cn: 想象一份裁决书被钉在木门上，永久封存。

examples.en: The peace treaty was made irrevocable by signatures from both sides.
examples.cn: 双方的签署使和平条约成为不可撤销的。

examples.en: Choosing a university can feel like an irrevocable step.
examples.cn: 选择大学可能让人感觉是无可挽回的一步。

examples.en: Her apology came too late for the damage, which had become irrevocable.
examples.cn: 她的道歉来得太晚，伤害已经无法挽回。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿不可了」——饿到这个地步就改不了主意了：拿谐音联想「不可改变」，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（否定）+ revocare（召回，由 re- 回 + vocare 呼唤）→ 晚期拉丁语 irrevocabilis（不可召回）→ 法语 irrévocable → 英语 irrevocable，核心义「叫不回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Irrevocable starts from a decision that cannot be called back, then covers results that cannot be undone and rulings that are final.
sensesIntro.cn: irrevocable 从「叫不回来的决定」出发，再扩展到「无法挽回的结果」与「终局裁决」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal already pressed, which cannot be taken back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚已经盖下的印章，再也收不回来。

branches.en: A formal decision that cannot be withdrawn is the core sense.
branches.cn: 无法撤回的正式决定是核心义。

branches.en: Consequences that cannot be reversed come from the same image.
branches.cn: 无法逆转的后果来自同一意象。

branches.en: A final ruling gives the word its legal sense.
branches.cn: 终局裁决使这个词有了法律义。

branches.en: Contracts and court rulings both become fixed once they are final.
branches.cn: 合同与法院裁决一旦终局就都固定下来。

branches.en: A final ruling and its lasting effects share the same permanence.
branches.cn: 终局裁决与其持久影响共享同一种永久性。

intro.en: Irrevocable is built from the negative prefix ir- and the Latin root voc- call, with revoke and revocable beside it.
intro.cn: irrevocable 由否定前缀 ir- 加拉丁词根 voc-（呼唤）构成，旁边站着 revoke 与 revocable。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare means to call, and revocare means to call back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare 意为呼唤，revocare 意为召回。

items.example: Vocare gives the root of voice and vocation.
items.exampleCN: vocare 提供 voice 与 vocation 的词根。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the idea of calling back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加上了「往回叫」的意思。

items.example: Revocare is the verb behind revoke.
items.exampleCN: revocare 是 revoke 背后的动词。

items.example: In- becomes ir- before the letter r.
items.exampleCN: in- 在字母 r 前变成 ir-。

items.example: The prefix ir- makes revocable negative.
items.exampleCN: 词缀 ir- 使 revocable 带上否定。

items.example: The suffix -able forms revocable from revoke.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 由 revoke 构成 revocable。

items.example: Revoke keeps the sense of calling back.
items.exampleCN: revoke 保留了「叫回来」的含义。

items.example: Revocable is the positive base of the negative form.
items.exampleCN: revocable 是带否定前缀形式的正面原形。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Vocation shares the calling root with irrevocable.
items.exampleCN: vocation 与 irrevocable 共享「呼唤」词根。

definition_zh: 易怒的；烦躁的；（身体部位）易受刺激的
definition_en: easily annoyed and quick to show anger
core_image: 一根被反复摩擦的神经：表面发红发热，一碰就跳起来
scene: 地铁晚点，车厢闷热，乘客回到家里。After a long delay on the train, he came home irritable and snapped at everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 irritable 是「易怒的」（第 1 个义项：容易生气、动不动就发火）；句意：火车晚点很久，他回到家烦躁易怒，对谁都发火。

pos.zh: （身体部位）易受刺激的；会发炎的

derivatives.zh: 易怒；烦躁；（身体）应激性，由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成
烦躁地；不耐烦地，由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成
使恼怒；刺激，是这个词去掉形容词后缀后的动词
刺激物；令人烦恼的事，来自同一拉丁词根

senses.title: Easily annoyed
senses.definition: getting annoyed quickly over small things
senses.definitionCN: 容易因为小事就生气
senses.example: Lack of sleep made her irritable all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足让她整个上午都烦躁易怒。
senses.why: The Latin verb irritare means to provoke, so an irritable person is one easily provoked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 irritare 意为刺激、激怒，所以易怒的人是一激就着的人。

senses.title: A tender body part
senses.definition: more sensitive than normal and quick to become inflamed
senses.definitionCN: 比正常更敏感，容易发炎或不适
senses.example: Doctors checked his irritable skin after the allergic reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 过敏反应之后，医生检查了他易受刺激的皮肤。
senses.why: The original physical sense of being irritated still lives in medical phrases.
senses.whyCN: 「被刺激」的原始身体意义仍保留在医学说法里。

senses.title: Caused by discomfort
senses.definition: showing temper because of heat, noise, or pain
senses.definitionCN: 因为炎热、噪音或疼痛而发脾气
senses.example: The crowded bus left everyone hot and irritable.
senses.exampleCN: 拥挤的公交让每个人都又热又烦。
senses.why: The mind mirrors the body: physical irritation turns into a short temper.
senses.whyCN: 心理映照身体：身体的刺激感会转化为脾气急躁。

intro.en: Irritable comes from Latin irritabilis, from irritare to provoke, and first entered English through a commentary on Latin rhetoric.
intro.cn: irritable 来自拉丁语 irritabilis，源于 irritare（激怒、刺激）；一般认为英语中先经拉丁修辞学注本的译语出现。

items.en: Irritare means to provoke or stir up anger.
items.cn: irritare 意为激怒、挑起怒气。

items.en: Irritabilis adds -bilis to mean able to be provoked.
items.cn: irritabilis 加上 -bilis，表示容易被激怒的。

items.en: English borrows the word as a learned medical and rhetorical term.
items.cn: 英语把它作为学术性的医学与修辞术语借入。

items.en: Doctors use it for nerves and muscles that react too quickly to stimulation.
items.cn: 医生用它描述对刺激反应过快的神经与肌肉。

items.en: Everyday speech extends it to a quick temper.
items.cn: 日常口语把它扩展到脾气急躁。

note.en: Irritable connects to the verb irritate and the noun irritation, and it sits among temper words such as cross and moody.
note.cn: irritable 与动词 irritate、名词 irritation 相连，并与 cross、moody 等脾气类词同处一个语义场。

entries.definition: to make someone annoyed
the feeling of annoyance
the quality of being easily annoyed
to supply land with water
entries.definitionCN: 灌溉；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: annoyed and ready to argue
often changing mood and often bad-tempered
irritable and impatient about small things

normalIntro.en: Irritable is built on irritate plus -able, so it literally means able to be irritated.
normalIntro.cn: irritable 由 irritate 加 -able 构成，字面意思就是「能被激怒的」。

normal.en: The verb irritate means to annoy someone on purpose or by accident.
normal.cn: 动词 irritate 意为有意或无意地惹恼某人。

normal.en: The suffix -able means able to receive the action.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 表示能够接受该动作。

normal.en: Irritable bowel syndrome is a common medical collocation.
normal.cn: irritable bowel syndrome 是常见的医学搭配。

normal.en: Adverbs and nouns change the ending to irritably and irritability.
normal.cn: 副词和名词形式分别换后缀，写成 irritably 和 irritability。

normal.en: Compare angry: angry can be a one-off reaction, irritable is a lasting tendency.
normal.cn: 对比 angry：angry 可以是一次性反应，irritable 是持续的倾向。

abstract.en: Imagine a wire rubbed again and again until a single touch makes it spark.
abstract.cn: 想象一根电线被反复摩擦，最后轻轻一碰就冒火花。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle that keeps whistling at the smallest flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶，遇到最小的火苗就尖声叫起来。

abstract.en: Think of an empty stomach growling at everyone nearby.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空空的胃，朝周围的人呼呼作响。

examples.en: He becomes irritable when he has to wait.
examples.cn: 他要排队等待时就变得烦躁。

examples.en: Illness often makes a child irritable and unwilling to eat.
examples.cn: 生病常让孩子烦躁不安、不愿进食。

examples.en: The nurse kept the room quiet so the irritable patient could rest.
examples.cn: 护士让房间保持安静，好让易怒的病人休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「易惹 tape 波」——容易被惹到，像碰到带电流的胶带一样炸一下：只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 irritare（刺激、激怒）→ irritabilis（易被激怒的）；一般认为英语先经拉丁修辞学注本的译词传入，核心义「一点就着」。

sensesIntro.en: Irritable begins with a quick temper, then returns to the body with sensitive parts, and finally links temporary discomfort to temper.
sensesIntro.cn: irritable 先表示脾气急躁，再回到身体指敏感易受刺激的部位，最后把一时的不适与脾气相连。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nerve that has been rubbed raw and reacts to the lightest touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被磨红的神经，最轻的一碰也会跳起。

branches.en: A quick temper is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 脾气急躁是日常义项。

branches.en: A tender body part keeps the physical sense.
branches.cn: 敏感的身体部位保留了身体义。

branches.en: Discomfort turning into temper shows the bridge between body and mood.
branches.cn: 不适变成坏脾气，显示身体与情绪的桥梁。

branches.en: Heat and noise make people both uncomfortable and irritable.
branches.cn: 炎热与噪音让人既不适又烦躁。

branches.en: Sensitive skin and a sensitive temper share one root of overreaction.
branches.cn: 敏感的皮肤与敏感的脾气共享「过度反应」这一根源。

intro.en: Irritable is the adjective of irritate, and the family also gives irritation, irritability, and the older irritant.
intro.cn: irritable 是 irritate 的形容词形式，同族还有 irritation、irritability 以及更早的 irritant。

latinIntro.en: Latin irritare means to excite or provoke, and -abilis marks what can be acted on.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 irritare 意为刺激、激怒，-abilis 表示可以承受该动作。

items.example: Irritare gives the family its provoking image.
items.exampleCN: irritare 提供这一词族的「激怒」意象。

items.example: The suffix -abilis shapes irritabilis.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -abilis 构成 irritabilis。

items.example: Irritate is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: irritate 是词族的基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -able turns irritate into irritable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把 irritate 变成 irritable。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms irritability.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 irritability。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms irritably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 irritably。

items.example: The noun irritation names both mood and skin.
items.exampleCN: 名词 irritation 既指情绪也指皮肤。

items.example: Irritant is the thing that provokes.
items.exampleCN: irritant 是引起刺激的事物。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms agent nouns such as irritant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成表示施动者的名词，如 irritant。

items.example: Biology also uses irritability for a response to stimuli.
items.exampleCN: 生物学也用 irritability 指对刺激的反应能力。

definition_zh: 恼怒；烦躁；刺激；（皮肤等的）发炎
definition_en: the feeling of being annoyed, or a sore condition of the skin
core_image: 皮肤上被反复擦红的一块：发痒、发热，让人忍不住去挠
scene: 新买的毛衣领口摸起来粗糙，贴了一整天。The rough collar rubbed his neck all day, and he ended up with an irritation that would not stop stinging.
sceneCN: 这里 irritation 是「刺激、发炎」（第 2 个义项：皮肤受刺激后的红痒）；句意：粗糙的衣领蹭了他一整天，最后脖子上起了一块止不住发痛的红痒处。

derivatives.zh: 使恼怒；刺激，是这个词的动词形式
易怒的；易受刺激的，由动词加形容词后缀 -able 构成
刺激物；惹人烦的事物，与动词同根

senses.title: The feeling of being annoyed
senses.definition: a feeling of slight anger or impatience
senses.definitionCN: 轻微生气或不耐烦的感觉
senses.example: She could not hide her irritation at the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她掩饰不住对延误的恼怒。
senses.why: The Latin verb irritare means to provoke, so the noun names the provoked feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 irritare 意为激怒，所以这个名词指被激起来的恼怒情绪。

senses.title: Soreness on the body
senses.definition: a painful or itchy sore area on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上疼痛或发痒的炎症区域
senses.example: The cream soothed the irritation on his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 药膏缓解了他手臂上的红肿。
senses.why: The word keeps its older physical meaning of a part being rubbed raw.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了原有的身体意义，指某一部位被磨得发红发痛。

senses.title: Something that annoys
senses.definition: a small thing that keeps annoying you
senses.definitionCN: 不断让人心烦的小事
senses.example: Constant noise is a common irritation in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 持续的噪音是办公室里常见的烦扰。
senses.why: By a shift of focus, the noun can also name the object that produces the annoyance.
senses.whyCN: 焦点一转移，这个名词也可以指产生恼怒的对象，即「烦人事」。

intro.en: Irritation comes from the Latin action noun irritatio, from irritare to provoke, translated in English from Latin rhetorical texts.
intro.cn: irritation 来自拉丁语动作名词 irritatio，源于 irritare（激怒）；一般认为英语先经拉丁修辞学注本的译语传入。

items.en: Irritare means to stir up or provoke.
items.cn: irritare 意为激怒、挑起。

items.en: The suffix -tio forms the noun irritatio, the act of provoking.
items.cn: 后缀 -tio 构成名词 irritatio，指激怒这一动作。

items.en: Learned English translates it as a rhetorical and medical term.
items.cn: 学术英语把它译作修辞与医学术语。

items.en: Medical writing uses it for inflamed or sensitive tissue.
items.cn: 医学写作用它指发炎或敏感的组织。

items.en: Everyday speech extends it to mild daily annoyances.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到日常的轻度烦扰。

note.en: Irritation is the noun partner of irritate and irritable, and it is close to words for annoyance and inflammation.
note.cn: irritation 是 irritate 与 irritable 的名词伙伴，与表示「烦扰」和「发炎」的词相近。

normalIntro.en: Irritation is the action noun of irritate, using the classic Latin -tion ending.
normalIntro.cn: irritation 是 irritate 的动作名词，使用经典的拉丁 -tion 后缀。

normal.en: The verb irritate means to provoke or annoy, and -tion makes it a feeling or a thing.
normal.cn: 动词 irritate 意为激怒、刺激，-tion 使它变成情绪或事物。

normal.en: Medical English uses irritation for redness and soreness of skin or eyes.
normal.cn: 医学英语用 irritation 指皮肤或眼睛的红肿与不适。

normal.en: In irritation describes speaking in an annoyed manner.
normal.cn: in irritation 指出以恼怒的方式说话。

normal.en: The whole family is irritate, irritating, irritated, irritation, and irritable.
normal.cn: 整个词族是 irritate、irritating、irritated、irritation 与 irritable。

normal.en: Compare annoyance: annoyance names the mood, irritation may also name a physical sore.
normal.cn: 对比 annoyance：annoyance 只指情绪，irritation 还可以指身体上的红痛。

abstract.en: Imagine a rough seam rubbing a small patch of skin until it turns pink.
abstract.cn: 想象一道粗糙的接缝反复摩擦一小块皮肤，一直磨到发红。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito bite on your ankle, itching so much you cannot sit still.
abstract.cn: 想象脚踝上被蚊子叮了一个包，痒得坐立不安。

abstract.en: See a tiny stone in your shoe, tiny but impossible to ignore.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里有一颗小石子，很小却让人无法忽视。

examples.en: He spoke with clear irritation about the broken printer.
examples.cn: 他谈到坏掉的打印机时语气明显带着烦躁。

examples.en: Chemicals in the detergent can cause skin irritation.
examples.cn: 洗涤剂中的化学物质可能刺激皮肤。

examples.en: Her calm manner eased the irritation among the passengers.
examples.cn: 她沉着的态度缓解了乘客中的烦躁情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一惹态甚」——一被惹到，姿态就变得很糟：用谐音联想「发火」，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 irritare（刺激、激怒）+ -tio（名词后缀）→ irritatio（激怒）；一般认为英语先经拉丁修辞学注本的译词传入，再由情绪义扩展到身体发炎义。

sensesIntro.en: Irritation moves from the feeling of being provoked to the physical soreness of skin, and then to the annoying thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: irritation 从「被激起的恼怒」出发，再到皮肤的红肿不适，最后指令人烦心的事物本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a patch of skin rubbed raw by a rough collar.
core.cn: 核心意象：被粗糙衣领磨得通红发痛的一小片皮肤。

branches.en: The mood of slight anger is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 轻微恼怒的情绪是日常义项。

branches.en: Soreness of skin keeps the physical sense.
branches.cn: 皮肤红肿保留了身体义。

branches.en: The noun can also name the nuisance that causes the feeling.
branches.cn: 这个名词也能指造成该感觉的烦扰事物。

branches.en: Both a bad mood and inflamed skin share the idea of being rubbed the wrong way.
branches.cn: 坏情绪与发炎的皮肤都共享「被反向摩擦」的观念。

branches.en: A chemical irritant links a physical sore and a daily nuisance.
branches.cn: 化学刺激物把身体的红痛与日常烦恼连在一起。

intro.en: Irritation uses the Latin noun suffix -tion on the root irritat-, and the family includes irritate, irritable, and irritant.
intro.cn: irritation 在词干 irritat- 上加拉丁名词后缀 -tion，同族词有 irritate、irritable 与 irritant。

latinIntro.en: Latin irritare means to provoke, and -tio turns a verb into the name of an action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 irritare 意为激怒，-tio 把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: Irritare supplies the verb root of the family.
items.exampleCN: irritare 提供词族的动词词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的词缀
items.example: The suffix -tio forms the Latin noun irritatio.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tio 构成拉丁名词 irritatio。

items.example: The suffix -tion gives the English noun irritation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 形成英语名词 irritation。

items.example: Irritate is the verb that the noun comes from.
items.exampleCN: irritate 是这个名词所来自的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ate marks the verb ending of irritate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 标记 irritate 的动词词尾。

items.example: The -ing form describes something that provokes.
items.exampleCN: -ing 形式描述引起恼怒的事物。

items.example: The -ed form describes a person who feels annoyed.
items.exampleCN: -ed 形式描述感到恼火的人。

items.example: The suffix -able adds the ability to be provoked.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 加上「容易被激怒」的能力含义。

items.example: The suffix -ant makes an agent noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成施动名词。

items.example: The suffix -ity names the quality behind irritation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 表示 irritation 背后的性质。

definition_zh: 岛民；岛屿居民；(Islander) 岛国人；海岛的原住岛民
definition_en: a person who lives on an island, or who belongs to an island community
core_image: 小岛上一间朝海的木屋，屋前站着长年不走的人
scene: 渡轮靠岸，码头边有人问起岛上的人家，老人指着山坡上的菜园。Every islander on the quay knew the ferry schedule by heart.
sceneCN: 这里 islander 是「岛民、岛屿居民」（第 1 个义项：住在岛上的人）；句意：码头上的每个岛民都把渡轮的班次记得清清楚楚。

derivatives.zh: 基础词：岛；加 -er 构成「岛上的居人」
island 加 -ing 构成，指把物体做成孤岛状的动作
对照词：陆地居民，islander 的反向成员

senses.title: A person who lives on an island
senses.definition: someone whose home and daily life are on an island
senses.definitionCN: 家与日常生活都在岛上的人
senses.example: Most islanders make their living from fishing and tourism.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数岛民靠捕鱼和旅游业谋生。
senses.why: The English noun island plus the agent suffix -er builds a person who belongs to that place.
senses.whyCN: 英语名词 island 加表「人」的后缀 -er，直指住在岛上的人，意象最直接。

senses.title: An inhabitant of a small community by the sea
senses.definition: an island native whose work is tied to the sea, such as fishing or farming
senses.definitionCN: 岛上原住民，工作与海相关，如捕鱼或农耕
senses.example: The old islanders still repair their nets on the beach at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 老海岛居民天一亮还在沙滩上补渔网。
senses.why: Islands usually have small, closely knit settlements, so the label also carries a sea-bound way of life.
senses.whyCN: 岛屿聚落通常规模小、人情近，所以这个词也带上「靠海为生」的生活方式色彩。

senses.title: A member of a named island people
senses.definition: a member of a people living on a particular island, often written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定岛屿上民族的成员，正式语境常大写
senses.example: He joined a club for islanders from the northern isles.
senses.exampleCN: 他加入了一个由北方各岛屿岛民组成的俱乐部。
senses.why: With a capital letter the word names a group identity, the way a region names its people.
senses.whyCN: 词首大写时，它指的是群体身份，如同用地区名来称呼当地人。

senses.title: A person shaped by a bounded, isolated world
senses.titleCN: 孤处受限的人；视野狭隘者
senses.definition: often in figurative use, a person whose outlook is limited by living in one small closed place
senses.definitionCN: 多用于比喻，指因长期生活在封闭小地方而眼界受限的人
senses.example: Critics called him an islander of ideas, kind but cut off from new currents.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称他为思想上的孤岛居民，善良却与新的潮流隔绝。
senses.why: The image is a land ringed by water: the physical boundary of an island turns into a mental boundary.
senses.whyCN: 意象是四面环水的陆地：岛的地理边界被引申为心理边界。

intro.en: Islander is a native English compound of island with the agent suffix -er, first recorded in the early modern period.
intro.cn: islander 是英语自有构词：名词 island 加表人的后缀 -er，一般认为首见于近代早期。

items.en: Island is the Old English word for a piece of land surrounded by water; it is a native Germanic word, not borrowed from Latin insula.
items.cn: 古英语 island 指四面环水的一片陆地，是日耳曼语本土词，并非借自拉丁语 insula。

items.en: The initial s in island is generally explained as native German spelling rather than a Latin influence.
items.cn: 词首的 s 一般认为来自日耳曼语拼写习惯，而非拉丁语影响。

items.en: Island combines with the agent suffix -er in the plain English way, so the meaning is a person of the island.
items.cn: island 按英语常规与表人后缀 -er 结合，字面即「岛上的人」。

items.en: Islander spreads through travel and colonial writing, naming people of named islands and groups.
items.cn: islander 借旅行与殖民书写流传开来，用来称呼特定岛屿或岛族的人。

items.en: The capitalised form serves as an identity label, and the figurative sense of a closed outlook develops in literary criticism.
items.cn: 现代英语里大写形式成为身份标签，评论文字中又长出「闭塞眼界」的比喻义。

note.en: Islander sits at the centre of a whole island family, and is close in meaning to resident and mainlander.
note.cn: islander 处在一整个「岛」词族的中心，语义上又与居民、大陆居民相邻。

entries.definition: a piece of land surrounded by water
an island, often a small one
entries.definitionCN: 小岛（多用于地名或文学作品）

entries.definition: a person who lives on the mainland
a person who lives in a particular place
a person born in a place, especially an indigenous one
a person or animal that lives in a place

normalIntro.en: Islander is built on plain English pieces: island, the person suffix -er, and a small island life.
normalIntro.cn: islander 由最普通的零件拼成：island、表人的 -er，以及小岛生活本身。

normal.en: Islander is island plus -er, the same suffix as in New Yorker, so it means a person of the island.
normal.cn: islander 就是 island 加 -er，和 New Yorker 的后缀一样，意为「岛上的人」。

normal.en: Its family includes the adjective island adjective islandwide, as in islandwide ferry service.
normal.cn: 同族词包括由 island 派生的形容词 islandwide，如全岛渡轮服务。

normal.en: Mainlander is its mirror image, a person of the mainland instead of the sea.
normal.cn: mainlander 是它的镜像词，指大陆一侧的人而非海岛一侧。

normal.en: The plural islanders is the common form in news about storms and ferries.
normal.cn: 在关于风暴与渡轮的新闻里，复数 islanders 最常见。

normal.en: Compare isle: an isle is the little land lot on the water, an islander is whoever lives on it.
normal.cn: 对比 isle：isle 是水面上的那块小地，islander 是住在上面的人。

abstract.en: See a wooden house facing the sea, with one stoop that never moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一间朝海的木屋，门前一级石阶多年不动。

abstract.en: See nets drying on a fence, repaired by the same hands every dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象栅栏上晾着渔网，每天天亮由同一双手修补。

abstract.en: See a whole people squeezed into one small ring of land inside the blue.
abstract.cn: 想象一整个族群，被蓝色包围在小小一圈陆地上。

examples.en: Islanders often have to cross to the mainland for special treatment.
examples.cn: 岛民常要渡海到大陆接受专科治疗。

examples.en: The island community held a festival for visitors every summer.
examples.cn: 这个岛屿社区每年夏天都为访客举办节日。

examples.en: Many Pacific islander families moved to cities for work.
examples.cn: 许多太平洋岛民家庭为了工作迁往城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记成「爱兰得」——island 加 -er，岛上守着菜园的人就是岛民；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: island（古英语本土词，四面环水的陆地）+ -er（表人后缀）→ islander（岛民）；与拉丁语 insula 无直接继承关系，只是意义对应。

sensesIntro.en: Islander starts as the plain person of an island, then sharpens into a sea-bound native, a named island people, and finally a metaphor for a closed outlook.
sensesIntro.cn: islander 先指最朴素的「岛上的人」，再细化为靠海为生的海岛居民、特定岛族成员，最后引申为眼界闭塞的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small house on an island, its owner never leaving.
core.cn: 核心意象：小岛上一间木屋，屋主从没搬走。

branches.en: The person sense is the literal unit of the map.
branches.cn: 「人」这一层是整张图的字面起点。

branches.en: The sea-bound life sense adds the texture of daily work.
branches.cn: 靠海为生的义项补上了日常劳作的质地。

branches.en: The capitalised sense turns the person into a group identity.
branches.cn: 大写形式把个体转成群体身份。

branches.en: The figurative sense carries the boundary from land to mind.
branches.cn: 比喻义把地理边界搬到了心里。

branches.en: Both point back to the physical island, one as a home, the other as a livelihood.
branches.cn: 两者都回到那座实体的岛，一为家，一为生计。

intro.en: Islander is a native English compound, so its parts are the Germanic word island and the agent suffix -er, plus look-alike isle words.
intro.cn: islander 是英语本土复合词，零件是日耳曼词 island、表人后缀 -er，以及一批外形相近的 isle 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin insula means island, and its adjective insularis gives English insular; it is a distant look-alike rather than a direct ancestor of island.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 insula 意为岛屿，其形容词 insularis 带来英语 insular；它与 island 只是远亲形近，并非直接来源。

definition_zh: 岛；小岛；屿（多用于地名或文学）
definition_en: an island, especially a small one, used chiefly in place names and literary writing
core_image: 海平面上浮起一小块绿色陆地，浪花围着它打转
scene: 地图上有个细小的名字，旁边画着一圈海岸线。From the cliff we could see a green isle floating in the blue sea.
sceneCN: 这里 isle 是「小岛、岛屿」（第 1 个义项：文学作品与地名里的小岛）；句意：从崖上我们看见一座绿色小岛浮在蔚蓝海面上。

collocations.zh: 绿宝石岛（爱尔兰的别称）

同一词族：住在 island 或 isle 上的人
平行词 island 的复数，义为「群岛、岛屿」

senses.title: An island, chiefly in literary use
senses.definition: an island, especially a small one, used in poetry and classic travel writing
senses.definitionCN: 小岛，尤指面积不大者，常见于诗歌与古典游记
senses.example: The lover watched her sailing toward a distant isle.
senses.exampleCN: 恋人望着她驶向一座遥远的岛。
senses.why: Isle and island share one origin, but isle kept the shorter Old French form and so sounds literary.
senses.whyCN: isle 与 island 同源，但 isle 保留了更短的古法语词形，因而带上文学色彩。

senses.title: A name element for a single island
senses.definition: the short island word used inside British and Irish place names
senses.definitionCN: 英国与爱尔兰地名中用来指岛的短词
senses.example: The Isle of Wight is famous for its cliffs and summer festivals.
senses.exampleCN: 怀特岛以悬崖和夏季音乐节闻名。
senses.why: Compact forms survive in place names long after everyday speech drops them, so isle lives on in geography.
senses.whyCN: 紧凑的词形在日常口语弃用后仍留在地名里，于是 isle 在地理名称中延续。

senses.title: A small tract like an island
senses.titleCN: 小片孤立之地；孤岛式区域
senses.definition: a small area that stands apart from its surroundings, as if it were an island
senses.definitionCN: 与周围区别开来的小块地方，如同被水隔开
senses.example: The old mill stands on an isle of cobblestone amid the parking lots.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老磨坊立在停车场中间一小块铺石的「孤岛」上。
senses.why: The core image is land fenced off by water; any fenced-off patch can borrow it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是被水围起的一片地，任何被围起来的小块都能借用这个意象。

senses.title: A far-off dream place
senses.titleCN: 遥远的梦幻之地；心之所向
senses.definition: a distant, idealised place that one longs for, almost a paradise
senses.definitionCN: 一个可望而不可即的理想之地，近乎乐园
senses.example: In his letters home he called the hillside cottage a sunny isle.
senses.exampleCN: 在家书里他把山坡小屋称作阳光灿烂的乐岛。
senses.why: A place cut off by sea becomes a place apart from ordinary troubles, and so a dream retreat.
senses.whyCN: 被海隔开的地方也就远离日常烦扰，于是成了梦中的栖身之地。

intro.en: Isle comes through Old French from Latin insula, island; the s was once pronounced, so the written s survives although the sound was dropped.
intro.cn: isle 经由古法语来自拉丁语 insula（岛）；词中的 s 一度是发音的，后来读音消失而拼写留下。

items.en: Insula is the classical Latin noun for island and the direct source of the word family.
items.cn: insula 是古典拉丁语表示「岛屿」的名词，也是该词族的直接来源。

items.en: Insula descends from a reconstructed Earlier Latin form generally written inisula, showing that the s once followed the n.
items.cn: 一般认为是早期拉丁语的重构形式 inisula 演变而来，说明 s 原本跟在 n 之后。

items.en: Old French keeps the form isle, with a pronounced s, and passes it into English.
items.cn: 古法语保留 isle 这一词形，s 当时仍发音，并由此传入英语。

items.en: Middle English adopts il or yle from the French, and the s is already silent in speech.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 il 或 yle 等写法，此时口语中的 s 已不发音。

items.en: Renaissance spelling restores the Latin s, though it stays silent, giving the modern isle.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的仿古拼写把拉丁语 s 补回来，但读音仍不发音，形成今天的 isle。

note.en: Isle is the short, literary island word; its exact look-alikes include aisle and the dimunitive islet, while near meanings include atoll and islet.
note.cn: isle 是简短而带文学气的「岛」，形近词有 aisle 与指小的 islet，近义词有环礁与礁岛。

normalIntro.en: Isle is the silent-s cousin of island: it came from Latin insula through Old French, and works mostly in place names and poems.
normalIntro.cn: isle 是 island 的「静音 s」表亲：经古法语来自拉丁语 insula，多用于地名与诗歌。

normal.en: Isle and island share the Latin insula, so both really contain the letter s that is no longer heard.
normal.cn: isle 与 island 共享拉丁语 insula，因此都含有已经不再发音的 s。

normal.en: Isle plus the dimunitive -et gives islet, a smaller island.
normal.cn: isle 加指小后缀 -et 得到 islet，指更小的岛。

normal.en: In place names it is always short: Isle of Man, Isle of Wight, Isle of Skye.
normal.cn: 在地名里它总是很短：马恩岛、怀特岛、天空岛。

normal.en: The Emerald Isle is a nickname for Ireland, so the word also names a whole country.
normal.cn: 绿宝石岛是爱尔兰的别称，可见这个词也能指整个国家。

normal.en: Compare aisle: same sound, same letter order, but aisle is a walkway, not an island.
normal.cn: 对比 aisle：读音相同、字母顺序相同，但 aisle 是过道，不是岛。

abstract.en: See a small green patch floating on a sheet of blue glass.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝玻璃似的海面浮着一小块绿斑。

abstract.en: See the map name drawn thin and small, with a ring of coast dots.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一个又细又小的名字，旁边一圈海岸线小点。

abstract.en: See a cobbled square standing alone between grey parking lots.
abstract.cn: 想象一块铺石小广场孤零零夹在灰色停车场之间。

examples.en: The isle is cut off by storms for weeks each winter.
examples.cn: 这座小岛每年冬天都会被风暴隔绝好几周。

examples.en: Many old houses on the isles are now holiday cottages.
examples.cn: 各小岛上的许多老屋如今成了度假小屋。

examples.en: Sailors once feared the rocks around that lonely isle.
examples.cn: 水手们曾害怕那座孤岛周围的礁石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记成「矮欧」——读音像「爱」，小岛总被海爱着；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 insula（岛）→ 早期拉丁语重构形式 inisula → 古法语 isle → 中古英语 il、yle → 近代补写 s 成为 isle；与 island 同源但写法不同。

sensesIntro.en: Isle begins as a literary island, settles as a place-name unit, then stretches to any island-like patch and to a dream retreat.
sensesIntro.cn: isle 先是一个文学化的「岛」，继而成为地名构词单位，再引申为任何像岛的小块，最后成为梦中乐土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small green island floating on the open sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块绿岛浮在开阔海面上。

branches.en: The literary island is the first everyday sense of the map.
branches.cn: 文学化的小岛是语义图的第一层日常义项。

branches.en: Place names freeze the short form into geography.
branches.cn: 地名把短词形冻结进地理名称。

branches.en: Any separated patch can borrow the island image.
branches.cn: 任何被隔开的小块都能借用岛的形象。

branches.en: The dream retreat is the remote island of the heart.
branches.cn: 梦幻之地是心中的遥远小岛。

branches.en: Both keep the old literary tone, one as landscape and one as longing.
branches.cn: 两者都保留旧的文学腔，一写景致，一写向往。

intro.en: Isle is a short Latin loanword, and the dimunitive -let on isle gives the smaller word islet; isle also partners with island and islander in the same family.
intro.cn: isle 是简短的拉丁借词，isle 加指小后缀 -let 得到更小的 islet；它还与 island、islander 同属一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin insula is the parent of isle, island, islet and insular; the Italian form isola and the Spanish isla are close relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 insula 是 isle、island、islet、insular 的共同源头，意大利语 isola 与西班牙语 isla 是近亲。

definition_zh: 小岛；礁岛；(解剖) 胰岛；(块状组织) 小岛状小区
definition_en: a very small island, or a small separate area of tissue or land
core_image: 海面上一块小得像礁石、只站得下几株草的陆地
scene: 浅滩尽头露出几块长草的礁石，渔船要绕着它走。Few boats dare to pass the islet when the tide is low.
sceneCN: 这里 islet 是「小岛、礁岛」（第 1 个义项：极小的岛屿）；句意：退潮时很少有船敢从这座小礁岛旁通过。

senses.title: A very small island
senses.definition: a very small island, often too small for settlement
senses.definitionCN: 面积很小的岛屿，常小到无法居住
senses.example: A lone palm grows on the islet in the middle of the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 海湾中央的小岛上长着一棵孤零零的棕榈树。
senses.why: Isle plus the dimunitive suffix -let means little island, so the size is built into the word.
senses.whyCN: isle 加指小后缀 -let 就是「小岛」，大小直接写在构词里。

senses.title: A small rocky or coral island
senses.definition: a small rocky or coral island rising just above the sea
senses.definitionCN: 刚露出海面的礁石或珊瑚小岛
senses.example: Gulls nest on the rocky islets off the northern coast.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥在北部海岸外的礁石小岛上筑巢。
senses.why: Because islets are tiny, they are often bare rock, so the word naturally names reef and coral outcrops.
senses.whyCN: 小岛往往只是裸岩，词义于是自然指向礁石与珊瑚礁。

senses.title: A small isolated area within something larger
senses.definition: a small patch that is separated from the surrounding area
senses.definitionCN: 与周围区域隔开的一小块地方
senses.example: A small islet of grass survives between the grey towers of concrete.
senses.exampleCN: 灰色混凝土塔楼之间还剩一小块草地。
senses.why: The image is a landmass cut off from the main body, so any separated patch can be called an islet.
senses.whyCN: 意象是被主体隔开的一小块陆地，因此任何被隔开的碎块都可以叫小岛。

senses.title: A group of cells in the pancreas
senses.definition: a cluster of hormone-releasing cells in the pancreas
senses.definitionCN: 胰腺中成团分布、负责分泌激素的细胞
senses.example: The islets of Langerhans release insulin into the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 朗格汉斯胰岛把胰岛素释放进血液。
senses.why: Under a microscope the cell clusters look like islands in a sea of tissue, so early anatomists reused the word.
senses.whyCN: 显微镜下这团细胞像组织之海里的小岛，早期解剖学家就借用了这个词。

intro.en: Islet is isle plus the French-inspired dimunitive -let; by spelling analogy people later wrote an s that had never been spoken.
intro.cn: islet 是 isle 加带法语色彩的指小后缀 -let；后来人们受 isle 拼写类比影响，加了原本从不发音的 s。

items.en: Old French isle carries the Latin island word into English.
items.cn: 古法语 isle 把拉丁语中的「岛」带入英语。

items.en: The dimunitive suffix -et, from Latin -ittus, appears in Old French and spreads to English.
items.cn: 指小后缀 -et 源自拉丁语 -ittus，见于古法语，后又进入英语。

items.en: Islet is formed as isle plus -et, literally a little isle.
items.cn: islet 由 isle 加 -et 构成，字面即「小岛」。

items.en: By analogy with isle, an s is inserted in spelling, giving islet, though no s sound is spoken.
items.cn: 受 isle 的拼写类比影响，词中补入 s，形成 islet，但口语中并不发出 s 音。

items.en: Medicine borrows the word for cell clusters in the pancreas, the islets of Langerhans.
items.cn: 现代英语的医学领域借这个词指胰腺中的细胞团，即朗格汉斯胰岛。

note.en: Islet is the dimunitive of isle and is confused with aiste and aisle, while its near meanings run from reef to atoll.
note.cn: islet 是 isle 的指小形式，容易与 aisle、inlet 混淆，近义词从礁石分布到环礁。

normalIntro.en: Islet follows a simple build: the island word isle plus the dimunitive -let, and the s is silent in spelling.

normal.en: Isle plus -let gives islet, the same -let as in booklet and droplet.
normal.cn: isle 加 -let 得到 islet，-let 与 booklet、droplet 里的后缀相同。

normal.en: The s in islet is silent, so speak it as eye-let.
normal.cn: islet 中的 s 不发音，读起来像 eye-let。

normal.en: Its plural islets appears in coast surveys and in anatomy.
normal.cn: 复数 islets 常见于海岸测绘与解剖学文本。

normal.cn: 朗格汉斯胰岛是以解剖学家命名、位于胰腺里的细胞小岛。

normal.cn: 对比 isle：isle 泛指小岛，islet 指刚露出水面、更小的那种。

abstract.en: See a rock just wide enough for a few tufts of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一块岩石，刚够长几丛草。

abstract.en: See gulls standing on black sea rocks, the tide boiling around them.
abstract.cn: 想象海鸥站在黑色礁石上，潮水在四周翻腾。

abstract.en: See a tiny patch of grass cut off between grey towers.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色塔楼之间被隔开的一小片草地。

examples.en: The islet disappears beneath the waves at high tide.
examples.cn: 涨潮时这座小岛会被海浪吞没。

examples.en: Several islets form a fragile barrier that protects the lagoon.
examples.cn: 几座小岛组成一道脆弱的屏障，守护着潟湖。

examples.en: Researchers traced how islets in the pancreas respond to sugar.
examples.cn: 研究人员追踪了胰岛对糖分的反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记成「小列特」——isle 加指小后缀 -let，就是更小的一小块；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 isle（岛，源自拉丁语 insula）+ 指小后缀 -et（源自拉丁语 -ittus）→ 小岛 islet；后受 isle 拼写类比补入不发音的 s。

sensesIntro.en: Islet grows from the literal little island, to bare reef and coral outcrops, then to any isolated patch, and at last to cell islands in the body.
sensesIntro.cn: islet 先从字面的小岛出发，扩展为裸露的礁石与珊瑚小岛，再泛指任何孤立小块，最后落到体内的小岛状细胞团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rock barely above the waves, with a few tufts of grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚高出水面的岩石，上面长着几丛草。

branches.en: The plain little island is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 最朴素的小岛是字面义。

branches.en: Bare rock and coral refine the island into a reef term.
branches.cn: 裸岩与珊瑚把「岛」细化成礁石术语。

branches.en: The isolated patch extends the shape beyond geography.
branches.cn: 孤立小块把形态引申出地理之外。

branches.en: The cell cluster is the body version of an islet.
branches.cn: 细胞团是「小岛」在人体里的对应。

branches.en: Both are tiny lands in water, one grassy and one bare.
branches.cn: 两者都是水中极小陆地，一有草，一裸露。

intro.en: Islet is a borrowed island word with a dimunitive suffix, so its parts are isle and -let, plus the island family that grew around them.
intro.cn: islet 是带指小后缀的「岛」类借词，零件是 isle 与 -let，并延展出整个 isle 词族。

latinIntro.en: Behind islet lie Latin insula for island and Latin -ittus for its dimunitive suffix; the Italian isola and Spanish isla share the same root.
latinIntro.cn: islet 背后是拉丁语 insula（岛）与源自拉丁语的指小后缀 -ittus，意大利语 isola 与西班牙语 isla 同出一源。

items.example: Isle is the base of islet.
items.exampleCN: isle 是 islet 的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -let makes islet smaller than isle.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -let 使 islet 比 isle 更小。

items.example: Islet is a little isle.
items.exampleCN: islet 就是一座小小的岛。

items.example: The suffix -itis names islet inflammation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -itis 表示胰岛炎症。

items.meaning: a hormone made by islet cells
items.example: Insulin comes from islet tissue.
items.exampleCN: 胰岛素来自胰岛组织。

items.example: Insular comes from Latin insula.
items.exampleCN: insular 来自拉丁语 insula。

items.meaning: a line of rock or coral under the sea
items.example: Reef is a near neighbour of islet.
items.exampleCN: reef 是 islet 的近邻词。

items.example: Atoll is a ring made of islets.
items.exampleCN: 环礁由许多小岛围成环形。

items.example: A cay is a sandy islet.
items.exampleCN: cay 是沙质的小岛。

latinEntries.example: Insula is the ancient source of the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: insula 是这个词的古老源头。

latinEntries.example: Insulae is the plural used in Roman texts.
latinEntries.exampleCN: insulae 是罗马文献里的复数形式。

latinEntries.example: Isola keeps the same root in Italian.
latinEntries.exampleCN: isola 在意大利语中保留同一词根。

definition_zh: 同位素；核素；示踪同位素
definition_en: a form of a chemical element whose atoms have the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons
core_image: 同一张脸，体重却不一样的一族兄弟
scene: 物理课上，老师用铅盒装着一小块样品，讲解它的两种变体在自然界里如何共存。In the physics class, the teacher passed round a sealed sample whose heavier isotope decays far more slowly than the lighter one.
sceneCN: 这里 isotope 是「同位素」（第 1 个义项：质子数相同而中子数不同的原子形式）；句意：在物理课上，老师传看一个密封样品，其中较重的那种同位素衰变比轻的慢得多。

derivatives.zh: 由 isotope 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「同位素的；同位素构成的」
由 isotope 与 geochemistry 复合而成，义为「同位素地球化学」
由 isotopic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「以同位素的方式」

senses.title: A form of an element
senses.definition: one of two or more forms of the same chemical element, differing only in neutron number
senses.definitionCN: 同一化学元素的两种或多种形式之一，区别只在原子核中的中子数
senses.example: Carbon has three naturally occurring isotopes.
senses.exampleCN: 碳有三种天然存在的同位素。
senses.why: The core image is one chemical identity wearing different weights, so the word names a variant atom of the same element.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是同一种化学身份带着不同的体重，因此这个词指同一元素的另一种原子形态。

senses.title: Radioactive member of the family
senses.definition: an unstable isotope that gives off radiation as its nucleus breaks down
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定、会因原子核衰变而放出射线的同位素
senses.example: Doctors use a radioactive isotope to trace blood flow.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用放射性同位素追踪血流。
senses.why: Because member atoms can be unstable, the family sense branches into the medical and nuclear sense of a radioactive form.
senses.whyCN: 因为家族成员可能不稳定，所以同位素家族义自然分支出医学与核领域的放射性同位素义。

senses.title: A labelled tracer
senses.definition: a distinctive isotope used as a marker to follow atoms through a system
senses.definitionCN: 被用作标记物、以追踪原子在系统中去向的特殊同位素
senses.example: The team tagged the water with an isotope tracer.
senses.exampleCN: 团队给水体加上了同位素示踪剂。
senses.why: Weight difference is invisible chemistry but a visible signal, so a chosen isotope can act as a label.
senses.whyCN: 体重差异在化学上是看不见的，却能被仪器读出，所以选定的同位素可以充当标记。

intro.en: Isotope was coined in 1913 by the chemist Frederick Soddy from Greek isos, equal, and topos, place.
intro.cn: isotope 由化学家索迪于一九一三年根据希腊语 isos（相等）与 topos（位置）造出。

items.en: Isos means equal and topos means place or location.
items.cn: isos 意为相等，topos 意为地方或位置。

items.en: Soddy combined the two Greek stems into the new scientific term isotope.
items.cn: 索迪把两个希腊词根合成新的科学术语 isotope。

items.en: The name records that different atomic forms share one place in the periodic table.
items.cn: 这个名字记录了一个事实：不同的原子形式在周期表上占据同一个位置。

items.en: Isotope spreads from atomic physics into dating, medicine, and geology.
items.cn: isotope 从原子物理扩散到年代测定、医学与地质学。

items.en: Terms such as stable isotope and isotope ratio become standard in research writing.
items.cn: 稳定同位素、同位素比值等说法成为科研写作中的标准用语。

note.en: Isotope belongs to the atom family: compare isotope with ion and allotrope for spelling, and with nuclide for meaning.
note.cn: isotope 属于原子家族：拼写上与 ion、allotrope 相邻，意义上与 nuclide 最接近。

entries.definition: having the same osmotic pressure
entries.definitionCN: 等渗的；只是与 isotope 共享 iso- 前缀，词源不同

entries.definition: the same in all directions
entries.definitionCN: 各向同性的；拼写相近但后缀不同，词源不同

entries.definition: one of several physical forms of the same element
entries.definitionCN: 同素异形体；与 isotope 都描述同种元素的不同形态

entries.definition: a species of atom with a given number of protons and neutrons
entries.definitionCN: 核素；与 isotope 几乎同义，但更强调核子数

entries.definition: a radioactive isotope
a substance used to follow a process
entries.definitionCN: 示踪剂；同位素常被用作示踪剂

normalIntro.en: Isotope joins isos, equal, and topos, place: atoms in the same place of the periodic table.
normalIntro.cn: isotope 由 isos（相等）与 topos（位置）合成：在周期表上占据同一个位置的原子。

normal.en: Iso- means equal, as in isotope and isometric.
normal.cn: iso- 表示相等，如 isotope 与 isometric 中都是这个前缀。

normal.en: Topos means place, so isotope atoms share one place.
normal.cn: topos 表示位置，所以同位素原子共享同一个位置。

normal.en: The adjective is isotopic, built with the suffix -ic.
normal.cn: 形容词是 isotopic，由后缀 -ic 构成。

normal.en: A radioisotope is a radioactive isotope of an element.
normal.cn: radioisotope 是某元素的放射性同位素。

normal.en: Stable isotope and isotope ratio are common research collocations.
normal.cn: stable isotope 与 isotope ratio 是常见的科研搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a row of identical twins who differ only in body weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一排双胞胎，长相完全一样，只有体重不同。

abstract.en: See one red-hot brother who insists on shedding sparks.
abstract.cn: 想象其中一个兄弟浑身发烫，不断掉落火星。

abstract.en: Think of a dyed drop of water spreading through a clear tank.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴带颜色的水在透明水池里慢慢散开。

examples.en: Researchers measured the isotope ratio in the ice core.
examples.cn: 研究人员测量了冰芯中的同位素比值。

examples.en: Nitrogen has two stable isotopes, both found in soil.
examples.cn: 氮有两种稳定同位素，都能在土壤中找到。

examples.en: The lab stores each radioactive sample in a lead container.
examples.cn: 实验室把每份放射性样品存放在铅容器里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱搜托普」——爱搜遍每个「托普」（顶点位置），原来它们占的是同一个座；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 isos（相等）+ topos（位置）→ 科学拉丁语 isotope（同位置者）→ 英语 isotope，核心义「同一位置上的不同原子」。

sensesIntro.en: Isotope starts as a chemical class name, then extends to unstable forms that radiate and to chosen forms used as tracers.
sensesIntro.cn: isotope 先指化学上的类别名称，再扩展到会放出射线的不稳定形式，最后扩展到被选作示踪剂的特定形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: identical twins who differ only in body weight.
core.cn: 核心意象：长相完全相同、只有体重不同的双胞胎。

branches.en: The class name for variant forms is the base sense.
branches.cn: 指称同元素不同形态的类别名称是基础义项。

branches.en: Unstable members add the radiation sense.
branches.cn: 不稳定的成员添上放射性这一层意思。

branches.en: A chosen member becomes a visible marker.
branches.cn: 被选中的成员变成可读出的标记。

branches.en: A radioactive isotope is still an isotope of that element.
branches.cn: 放射性同位素仍然是该元素的同位素。

branches.en: Tracer work needs two isotopes of the same element.
branches.cn: 示踪工作需要同一元素的两种同位素作对照。

intro.en: Isotope is built on two Greek elements, iso- and -tope, with English forms such as isotopic and radioisotope.
intro.cn: isotope 由 iso- 与 tope（来自 topos）两个希腊成分构成，英语中有 isotopic、radioisotope 等形式。

latinIntro.en: Isotope is modern scientific coinage from Greek roots; Latin itself has no native word for it.
latinIntro.cn: isotope 是由希腊词根构成的现代科学新造词，拉丁语本身没有这个本族词。

items.example: The prefix iso- means equal.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 iso- 表示相等。

items.example: Topos supplies the place image.
items.exampleCN: topos 提供位置的意象。

items.example: Isotope ends in the element -tope.
items.exampleCN: isotope 以成分 -tope 结尾。

items.example: Isotope names the atomic family.
items.exampleCN: isotope 命名这一原子家族。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms isotopic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 isotopic。

items.example: Isotopic analysis reveals the sample age.
items.exampleCN: 同位素分析揭示样品年龄。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms isotopically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 isotopically。

items.example: The water was isotopically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这些水在同位素上可以区分。

items.example: Radio- forms radioisotope with isotope.
items.exampleCN: radio- 与 isotope 合构成 radioisotope。

items.example: A radioisotope emits radiation.
items.exampleCN: 放射性同位素会放出射线。

definition_zh: 行程；旅行路线；行程表
definition_en: a planned route for a journey, or a document listing the places to be visited and the times of travel
core_image: 一张写满站点的路线纸，从一个点到下一个点
scene: 出发前夜，桌上摊着一张手写的旅行路线单，每一站旁边都标好了时间。Before the trip, the guide folded the itinerary into a small booklet and handed a copy to each traveller.
sceneCN: 这里 itinerary 是「行程；行程表」（第 3 个义项：列出站点与时间的书面安排）；句意：出发前，导游把行程折成小册子，给每位旅客发了一份。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 itinerari 加形容词后缀 -ant 构成，义为「巡游的；流动的」
拉丁语原词，意为「旅行者」，是 itinerary 的直接来源
由前缀 pre- 与 itinerary 复合而成，义为「出发前拟定的行程草案」

senses.title: The route of a journey
senses.definition: the overall path a journey will follow from place to place
senses.definitionCN: 一次旅行从一个地方到另一个地方所走的整体路径
senses.example: The route follows an itinerary along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路线沿河而下。
senses.why: The core image is a line joining stops, so the first sense names the path itself, not the paper.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一条串起各站点的线，所以第一个义项指的是路径本身，而不是那张纸。

senses.title: A plan for the stops
senses.definition: the plan of when and where the traveller will stop and what will happen there
senses.definitionCN: 关于旅客何时何地停留、在那里做什么的安排
senses.example: The itinerary allows a free afternoon in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 行程安排里给这座城留了一个空闲的下午。
senses.why: Once the route is fixed, each stop needs a time, so the path sense grows into a schedule sense.
senses.whyCN: 路线一旦确定，每一站都需要时间安排，于是路径义生长为日程义。

senses.title: The printed or written document
senses.definition: a written or printed list of the places to be visited, often given to a traveller
senses.definitionCN: 书面列出要走访地点、常发给旅客的清单
senses.example: Please keep your itinerary with your passport.
senses.exampleCN: 请把行程表和护照放在一起。
senses.why: The Latin source names a traveller, and the modern noun has become the paper the traveller carries.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原词指旅行者，而现代名词已经转指旅行者随身携带的那张纸。

senses.title: A formal record of visits
senses.definition: a formal account of the places visited by an official or a representative
senses.definitionCN: 官方或代表出访所到之处的正式记录
senses.example: The report opens with a short itinerary of the visits.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头是一份简短的巡访记录。
senses.why: Official travel must be documented, so the neutral schedule sense hardens into a formal record.
senses.whyCN: 公务出行需要留档，于是中性的日程义固化为正式记录义。

senses.title: A list of works or readings
senses.definition: a list of texts, pieces, or topics to be presented or studied in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序要讲、要学或要演的作品与题目清单
senses.example: The seminar itinerary lists three papers for today.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨会的安排里列出今天要读的三篇论文。
senses.why: A walk from place to place and a walk through works share one logic, so the word extends to ordered lists of content.
senses.whyCN: 从一个地方走到另一个地方，与从一篇作品走到另一篇作品逻辑相同，于是这个词扩展到有序的内容清单。

intro.en: Itinerary comes from Latin itinerarium, an account of a journey, built on iter, a journey or way.
intro.cn: itinerary 来自拉丁语 itinerarium（旅途记述），词根是 iter（旅程；道路）。

items.en: Iter means a journey or a path taken on foot.
items.cn: iter 意为旅程或步行的路径。

items.en: Itinerarius describes something or someone that travels.
items.cn: itinerarius 描述与旅行有关的人或事物。

items.en: Itinerarium names a written guide to a route, such as a pilgrim road book.
items.cn: itinerarium 指书写成册的路线指南，如朝圣者用的小册。

items.en: Itinerary enters English as a record of travel.
items.cn: itinerary 在十五世纪进入英语，指旅行记录。

items.en: The word shifts from a record to a plan, and finally to the printed list handed to travellers.
items.cn: 这个词从记录转向计划，最终指发给旅客的印刷清单。

note.en: Itinerary shares its root with itinerary-like words such as itinerant, and is close in meaning to schedule and route.
note.cn: itinerary 与 itinerant、itinerate 同根，意义上与 schedule、route 最接近。

entries.definition: travelling from place to place, especially for work
to travel from place to place
lasting only a short time
entries.definitionCN: 短暂的；只是读起来相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a plan of times for events
the way from one place to another
a list of things to be done at a meeting

normalIntro.en: Itinerary is a journey on paper: the Latin iter, path, plus a noun ending for a written account.
normalIntro.cn: itinerary 是纸上的旅程：拉丁语 iter（路途）加上表示书面记述的名词词尾。

normal.en: The root iter means a journey, as in itinerary.
normal.cn: 词根 iter 意为旅程，itinerary 就出自它。

normal.en: An itinerant worker travels from job to job.
normal.cn: itinerant 形容不断换地方工作的人。

normal.en: The plural drops the y for i: itineraries.
normal.cn: 复数把词尾的 y 改为 i：itineraries。

normal.en: Draw up an itinerary before booking hotels.
normal.cn: 订酒店之前先拟定行程。

normal.en: Compare schedule, which fixes times, with itinerary, which fixes places.
normal.cn: 对比 schedule 定时间，itinerary 定地点。

abstract.en: Picture a dotted line hopping between pins on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上一条虚线在几个图钉之间跳跃。

abstract.en: See a neat timetable with each stop boxed in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张整齐的时刻表，每一站都装在一个小方格里。

abstract.en: Think of a folded paper peeking out of a traveller pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象旅客口袋里露出一角折好的行程单。

examples.en: Our itinerary includes two nights in the mountains.
examples.cn: 我们的行程包括在山里住两晚。

examples.en: The agent sent a revised itinerary after the flight was delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误后，代理发来了修改过的行程。

examples.en: She keeps every old itinerary as a souvenir.
examples.cn: 她把每一份旧行程单都留作纪念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱替你奈若利」——爱你，就替你安排奈若（无奈）的路线，一路一站一站写清楚；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 iter（旅程、道路）→ itinerarius（旅行的）→ itinerarium（旅途记述）→ 英语 itinerary，核心义「一路走去的站点安排」。

sensesIntro.en: Itinerary begins with the path of a journey, becomes the plan of stops, then the written paper, next an official record, and finally any ordered list.
sensesIntro.cn: itinerary 从旅行的路径开始，变为站点的安排计划，再变成为书面清单，接着指官方记录，最后泛指任何有序清单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a route line running from pin to pin on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上从一枚图钉连到另一枚图钉的路线。

branches.en: The path itself is the earliest sense.
branches.cn: 路径本身是最早的义项。

branches.en: Timed stops turn the path into a plan.
branches.cn: 给站点加上时间，路径就变成计划。

branches.en: The plan on paper becomes a travelling document.
branches.cn: 写在纸上的计划成为随身文件。

branches.en: Official trips turn the document into a record.
branches.cn: 公务出行把文件变成记录。

branches.en: An ordered list of stops works for works or topics too.
branches.cn: 有序的站点清单同样适用于作品与题目。

intro.en: Itinerary is built from the Latin root iter, journey, with the ending -ary, and English keeps the related forms itinerant and itinerate.
intro.cn: itinerary 由拉丁词根 iter（旅程）加词尾 -ary 构成，英语保留了 itinerant、itinerate 等同族形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin iter and its derived itinerarius, travelling, supply both the route image and the traveller image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iter（旅程）及其派生词 itinerarius（旅行的）同时提供了路线与旅行者两种意象。

items.example: Iter is the hidden root of itinerary.
items.exampleCN: iter 是 itinerary 隐藏的词根。

items.example: Itinerarius describes travel matters.
items.exampleCN: itinerarius 描述与旅行相关的事物。

items.example: Itinerarium is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: itinerarium 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms itinerary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 itinerary。

items.example: Itinerary keeps the route meaning.
items.exampleCN: itinerary 保留路线含义。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms itinerant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 itinerant。

items.example: An itinerant seller moves between towns.
items.exampleCN: 巡游的商贩在各镇之间走动。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms itinerate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 itinerate。

items.meaning: to travel from place to place
items.example: Judges once itinerated across the country.
items.exampleCN: 过去法官曾在全国巡回。

items.example: Pre- shows a plan made before travel.
items.exampleCN: pre- 表示出发前制定的计划。

definition_zh: 常春藤；爬藤植物；老牌名校
definition_en: a climbing plant with dark green leaves that clings to walls and trees, or a symbol of old universities
core_image: 一面石墙上爬满深绿色、紧贴墙面的藤叶
scene: 老房子的石墙上爬满藤叶，绿色的叶子一直铺到屋檐下。Every autumn the old wall turns dark green as the ivy tightens its grip on the stones.
sceneCN: 这里 ivy 是「常春藤」（第 1 个义项：紧贴墙面攀爬的常绿藤本植物）；句意：每到秋天，老墙就变成深绿色，因为常春藤把石头抓得更紧了。

collocations.zh: 常春藤联盟（美国东部名校联盟）

derivatives.zh: 由 ivy 加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「爬满常春藤的」
由 ivy 与 covered 复合而成，义为「被常春藤覆盖的」
由 ivy 与 leaved 复合而成，义为「叶形像常春藤的」

senses.title: The climbing plant
senses.definition: a green climbing plant with lobed leaves that holds on to walls, trees, or rocks
senses.definitionCN: 叶子呈裂片状、能附着在墙、树或岩石上的绿色攀缘植物
senses.example: The ivy has covered the whole north wall.
senses.exampleCN: 常春藤已经爬满了整面北墙。
senses.why: The core image is a wall turning green, so the first sense is simply the plant that does the covering.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是墙被染成绿色，所以第一个义项就是做这件事的植物本身。

senses.title: A leafy covering on stone
senses.definition: the mass of green leaves and stems that covers a wall and keeps it damp
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖墙面、使墙体保持潮湿的绿叶与藤蔓整体
senses.example: Thick ivy hides the cracks in the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的常春藤遮住了老墙上的裂缝。
senses.why: The core image is the wall being turned green, so besides the plant itself the word also names the green coating it forms.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是墙被染成绿色，因此除了植物本身，这个词也指它形成的绿色覆盖层。

senses.title: A sign of old age
senses.definition: a symbol of long practice or age, as seen on old stone buildings
senses.definitionCN: 长久传统或年代感的象征，常见于老石建筑上
senses.example: The ivy around the door makes the house feel old.
senses.exampleCN: 门边那圈常春藤让房子显得很有年代感。
senses.why: Because ivy grows slowly and lasts for years, the plant can stand for long practice and inherited tradition.
senses.whyCN: 因为常春藤长得慢、能活很多年，所以这种植物可以象征悠久传承与老传统。

senses.title: The old university elite
senses.definition: the group of old, long-established universities, especially in the north-east of the United States
senses.definitionCN: 历史悠久的老牌大学群体，尤指美国东北部的那几所
senses.example: He turned down an Ivy college for a local scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 他放弃了老牌名校，选择了本地的奖学金。
senses.why: Old colleges are often shown with ivy on their walls, so the plant became a shorthand for prestige and age.
senses.whyCN: 老校舍的墙上常有常春藤，于是这种植物成了声望与年代的代称。

intro.en: Ivy goes back to Old English ifig, with related forms in Old High German and Old Norse; the final spelling follows the Latin-looking ivy.
intro.cn: ivy 可追溯到古英语 ifig，古高地德语与古诺斯语中也有同族形式；现代拼写受拉丁外观影响定型为 ivy。

items.en: Ifig names the climbing plant in Old English texts.
items.cn: 古英语文献中 ifig 指这种攀缘植物。

items.en: Related forms such as ebiwaw appear in continental Germanic languages.
items.cn: ebiwaw 等同族形式出现在大陆日耳曼语中。

items.en: Spellings shift from iviestow direction to ivi and ive.
items.cn: 拼写在中期英语中先后作 ivi 与 ive。

items.en: The modern spelling ivy is fixed and the plant becomes a garden and churchyard favourite.
items.cn: 现代拼写 ivy 固定下来，这种植物成为花园与墓园的常见植物。

items.en: Ivy League names a group of old American universities and turns the plant into a cultural label.
items.cn: 常春藤联盟这一叫法把这种植物变成一种文化标签。

note.en: Ivy is a short plant name that looks like Ivey and Ive, and sits near other climbing plants such as vine and creeper.
note.cn: ivy 是短小的植物名，形近 Ivey、Ive 等拼写，义场上与 vine、creeper 邻近。

entries.definition: covered with ivy
a common family name spelled differently
entries.definitionCN: 常见的姓氏拼法；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the hard white material from elephant tusks
entries.definitionCN: 象牙；开头看起来相近，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a climbing or trailing plant
a plant that grows along the ground or up a surface
a plant that climbs walls or supports

normalIntro.en: Ivy is a very old Germanic plant word, short and green, with English relatives such as ivied and ivy-covered.
normalIntro.cn: ivy 是一个很古老的日耳曼语植物词，短小而青绿，英语中有 ivied、ivy-covered 等派生形式。

normal.en: The plural is ivies, with the y changed to ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 ivies，词尾 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: An ivied wall is a wall covered with green leaves.
normal.cn: ivied wall 指爬满绿叶的墙。

normal.en: Ivy League refers to old American universities in the north-east.
normal.cn: Ivy League 指美国东北部的一批老牌大学。

normal.en: Ivy is a climber with a small root-like grip on the wall.
normal.cn: 常春藤是攀缘植物，用像小根一样的装置抓住墙面。

normal.en: Compare vine: vine is any climbing stem, ivy is the dark green one.
normal.cn: 对比 vine：vine 泛指攀缘茎藤，ivy 特指深绿那种。

abstract.en: Picture a stone tower slowly turning into a green column.
abstract.cn: 想象一座石塔慢慢变成一根绿柱子。

abstract.en: See a green sheet laid over bricks, hiding every crack.
abstract.cn: 想象一张绿毯盖在砖墙上，把所有裂缝都遮住。

abstract.en: Think of a grey-haired doorkeeper who has stood in place for decades.
abstract.cn: 想象一位白发的守门人，几十年一直站在同一个位置。

examples.en: The ivy on the tower turns red at the edges in winter.
examples.cn: 塔上的常春藤在冬天叶边会变红。

examples.en: Leave a strip of wall free of ivy so the paint can dry.
examples.cn: 在墙上留一条不带常春藤的位置，好让油漆干透。

examples.en: The play was staged in an ivy garden behind the church.
examples.cn: 这出戏在教堂后面爬满常春藤的花园里上演。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱为」——常春藤爱为老墙遮风挡雨，缠着墙往上爬；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ifig（常春藤）→ 中古英语 ivi → 现代英语 ivy；与古高地德语 ebiwaw 等同源，一般认为源自日耳曼语族的植物名。

sensesIntro.en: Ivy names the green climbing plant, then borrows its image to label old elite universities.
sensesIntro.cn: ivy 先命名这种绿色攀缘植物，再借它的意象代指老牌名校。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone wall slowly painted green from the ground up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面石墙从地面起被慢慢涂成绿色。

branches.en: The plant itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 植物本身是日常义项。

branches.en: The leafy mass that covers a wall is its visible result.
branches.cn: 铺满墙面的藤叶是它可见的成果。

branches.en: Its slow growth gives it the mark of age.
branches.cn: 缓慢的生长使它带上岁月标记。

branches.en: Old colleges borrow that age for a prestige label.
branches.cn: 老牌大学借这份岁月感获得声望标签。

branches.en: All of them keep the picture of green leaves on old walls.
branches.cn: 这些义项都保留着老墙上绿叶的画面。

intro.en: Ivy is a native Germanic word rather than a Latin one, and English builds ivied and ivy-covered from it.
intro.cn: ivy 是日耳曼语本族词而非拉丁语词，英语在此基础上构出 ivied 与 ivy-covered。

latinIntro.en: Latin has hedera for the plant, but the English word ivy does not come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 hedera 指这种植物，但英语的 ivy 并非来自它。

items.example: Ivy is a native Germanic word.
items.exampleCN: ivy 是日耳曼语本族词。

items.example: The ivies on the gate are trimmed often.
items.exampleCN: 门上的常春藤经常修剪。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms ivied.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 ivied。

items.example: An ivied gate hides the lane.
items.exampleCN: 一扇爬满常春藤的门遮住了小路。

items.meaning: used as the first part of compounds
items.example: Ivy- often starts compound adjectives.
items.exampleCN: ivy- 常作复合形容词的开头。

items.example: Covered joins ivy to form a compound.
items.exampleCN: covered 与 ivy 组成复合词。

items.example: The ivy-covered hall is very old.
items.exampleCN: 那座爬满常春藤的礼堂很古老。

items.example: Leaved makes ivy-leaved.
items.exampleCN: leaved 构成 ivy-leaved。

items.example: Ivy League names a sports league.
items.exampleCN: 常春藤联盟最初指一个体育联盟。

definition_zh: 行话；专业术语；行业黑话；难懂的行内用语
definition_en: special words and phrases used by a particular profession or group, often hard for outsiders to understand
core_image: 一间只对内部人开门的屋子，门外的人只听见屋里一片听不懂的暗语
scene: 会议结束后，医生们围在一起低声交谈，满口缩写术语，家属站在门口一句也听不明白。After the briefing, the doctors fell into their own jargon and the anxious family could follow almost nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 jargon 是「行话、专业术语」（第 1 个义项：某一群体内部使用的特殊用语）；句意：简报结束后，医生们说起自己的行话，焦虑的家属几乎什么都听不懂。

pos.zh: 行话；专业术语；行业黑话；难懂的用语
行话的；用了行业术语的（较少见，多见于技术行话一类的组合）

derivatives.zh: 由 jargon 加后缀 -istic 构成，义为「满口行话的、术语式的」
由 jargon 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「爱用行话的人」
英式拼写，由 jargon 加动词后缀 -ise 构成，义为「用行话说话或写作」
美式拼写，与 jargonise 同义，义为「使用行话、术语满口」

senses.title: Special words of a group
senses.definition: the special words and expressions used within a particular profession, trade or group
senses.definitionCN: 某个行业、职业或群体内部使用的特殊词语和说法
senses.example: Every trade has its own jargon.
senses.exampleCN: 每个行业都有自己的行话。
senses.why: The word first meant the meaningless chatter of birds, so the speech of a closed group became its jargon.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指鸟的叽喳、听不懂的聒噪，于是一个封闭群体内部的说话方式就被叫作 jargon。

senses.title: Language outsiders cannot follow
senses.definition: a way of speaking aimed mainly at insiders, so that listeners outside the group cannot understand it
senses.definitionCN: 主要面向内部人的说话方式，以致群体之外的人听不懂
senses.example: To us, the talk at the counter sounded like a private jargon.
senses.exampleCN: 对我们来说，柜台边的谈话像是一套私下的黑话。
senses.why: Because the original image was unintelligible bird noise, jargon easily carries the sense of a closed code.
senses.whyCN: 因为原始意象就是听不懂的鸟鸣，jargon 很容易带上「封闭暗码」的含义，让外人被挡在语言门外。

senses.title: Wordy technical style
senses.definition: writing or speech that is stuffed with technical terms and is unclear or pompous
senses.definitionCN: 堆满技术术语、含糊或故作高深的文字与讲话
senses.example: Strip away the jargon and the report has little to say.
senses.exampleCN: 去掉那些术语堆砌，这份报告几乎没有内容。
senses.why: When insiders use group words outside the group, jargon becomes a style of vague, inflated language.
senses.whyCN: 当内部人把群体词用到群体之外，jargon 就从身份标记变成一种含糊而浮夸的文体。

intro.en: Jargon entered English from Old French, where it first described the twittering of birds before it named the speech of people.
intro.cn: jargon 从古法语进入英语，最初描述鸟的啁啾，后来才用来指人的说话方式。

items.en: The French word is generally linked to a form such as garrulare, to chatter.
items.cn: 一般认为，法语词与类似 garrulare 的形式有关，意为喋喋不休。

items.en: Jargon means the chattering or warbling of birds.
items.cn: 古法语 jargon 意为鸟的叽喳与婉转鸣叫。

items.en: It shifts to the speech of people, especially a strange or barbarous tongue.
items.cn: 它转而指人的说话方式，尤其指陌生或野蛮难懂的语言。

items.en: English borrows jargon for unintelligible speech or bird noise.
items.cn: 英语借入 jargon，指听不懂的言语或鸟叫声。

items.en: From the 17th century it settles on the special words of a trade or group.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，它稳定指某一行业或群体的特殊用语。

items.en: Today jargon also names pompous, term-heavy writing in editing and style guides.
items.cn: 如今在编辑与文体指南中，jargon 也指堆砌术语、故作高深的文字。

note.en: Jargon is the speech of a closed group, close in form to jangle and in meaning to slang and technical terms.
note.cn: jargon 是封闭群体的说话方式，形式上与 jangle 近似，意义上与 slang、technical terms 相邻。

entries.definition: to make a harsh ringing noise
entries.definitionCN: 发出刺耳的叮当声；与 jargon 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to grate on the ears or nerves
entries.definitionCN: （声音）刺耳、令人不快；与 jargon 首音相近，但词源不同

entries.definition: a channel at the roadside for rainwater
entries.definitionCN: 路边的排水沟；与 jargon 尾音相近，只是谐音联想，词源无关

entries.definition: very informal words used by a group, often young people
entries.definitionCN: 俚语，多为群体内部非常随意的说法

entries.definition: the body of terms used in a subject
entries.definitionCN: 术语系统；某一学科的专门用语总和

entries.definition: insincere or self-serving talk
entries.definitionCN: 假话；伪善的套话，也常指行话

normalIntro.en: Jargon begins as bird chatter: noise that only the birds themselves can follow.
normalIntro.cn: jargon 原本是鸟的叽喳：一种只有鸟自己才听得懂的声响。

normal.en: Technical jargon keeps specialists talking quickly to one another.
normal.cn: technical jargon 让专业人士之间可以飞快交流。

normal.en: Medical jargon often hides simple facts behind long Latin terms.
normal.cn: medical jargon 常用长长的拉丁术语把简单事实藏起来。

normal.en: To cut through the jargon is to explain something in plain language.
normal.cn: cut through the jargon 就是用大白话把事情说清楚。

normal.en: A report full of jargon reads as vague and self-important.
normal.cn: 满是术语的报告读起来既含糊又自命不凡。

normal.en: Compare slang: slang is casual group talk, jargon is professional or technical.
normal.cn: 对比 slang：slang 是随意的群体口语，jargon 偏专业、技术性的用语。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked only for members, with a crowd listening outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只对会员开放的门，门外一群人侧耳细听却听不懂。

abstract.en: Hear a flock of birds chattering, and then swap the birds for engineers.
abstract.cn: 听一群鸟在叽喳，再把鸟换成一群工程师，声音同样密不透风。

abstract.en: Imagine a fog of long words rolling over plain sentences until they disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象一团长词组成的雾碾过朴素的句子，直到句子彻底消失。

examples.en: The manual was written in dense technical jargon that few users understand.
examples.cn: 这份手册写满了密集的技术术语，很少有用户看得懂。

examples.en: Please avoid medical jargon when you explain the treatment to my parents.
examples.cn: 请在我父母面前讲解治疗方案时避免使用医学术语。

examples.en: Good teachers translate jargon into everyday examples.
examples.cn: 好老师会把行话翻译成日常例子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎梗」——话里一个接一个扎满硬梗，外人听得一头雾水，就是行话；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自古法语 jargon（鸟的叽喳），可能与中世纪拉丁语 garrulare（喋喋不休）相关，源自 garrulus（多话的）；核心义「外人听不懂的聒噪」→ 群体内部专用语；古法语词与拉丁语 garrulus 之间的联系属推定，词源细节尚有讨论。

sensesIntro.en: Jargon starts as unintelligible noise, then becomes the words of a group, then the closed code of outsiders, and finally a pompous technical style.
sensesIntro.cn: jargon 起初指听不懂的聒噪，后来指一个群体的专用词，再指对外封闭的暗码，最后指堆砌术语的浮夸文体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door for insiders, with outsiders hearing only noise.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇只对内部人开的门，门外的人只听见噪声。

branches.en: The dedicated words of a profession are the basic sense.
branches.cn: 某一职业的专门用语是基本义项。

branches.en: A closed code that shuts outsiders out is the social sense.
branches.cn: 把外人关在门外的封闭暗码是社交义项。

branches.en: Term-heavy, pompons writing is the critical sense.
branches.cn: 堆砌术语、浮夸难懂的写作是批评性义项。

branches.en: Every group word can serve both as a tool and as a barrier.
branches.cn: 每个群体词既可以是沟通工具，也可以是理解屏障。

branches.en: Jargon used on outsiders reads as a wall of vagueness.
branches.cn: 对外人使用行话，读起来就是一堵含糊的墙。

intro.en: Jargon comes from a French word for bird chatter, and English has built jargonist, jargonistic and jargonize around it.
intro.cn: jargon 来自法语中表示鸟鸣的词，英语围绕它构成了 jargonist、jargonistic 与 jargonize。

latinIntro.en: Latin garrulus, from garrire, means chattering or talkative, and is generally taken as the distant root of the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 garrulus 源自动词 garrire，意为叽喳、多话，一般认为它是法语词的远源。

items.meaning: the special words of a group
items.example: Jargon is the everyday word for group speech.
items.exampleCN: jargon 是表示群体用语的最常用词。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ist forms jargonist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 jargonist。

items.example: A jargonist speaks mostly to insiders.
items.exampleCN: 爱用行话的人主要只对内部人说话。

items.example: The suffix -istic forms jargonistic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -istic 构成 jargonistic。

items.example: Jargonistic text puts terms before readers.
items.exampleCN: 满口行话的文字把术语放在读者之前。

items.meaning: to make or act in a way
items.example: The suffix -ise forms jargonise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成 jargonise。

items.example: To jargonise is to hide plain facts in terms.
items.exampleCN: 用行话说话就是把简单事实藏进术语。

items.meaningCN: 与 -ise 同用的美式词尾
items.example: The suffix -ize forms jargonize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 jargonize。

items.example: Editors ask writers not to jargonize.
items.exampleCN: 编辑要求作者不要满口行话。

definition_zh: 茉莉；茉莉花；茉莉花香；茉莉味
definition_en: a climbing shrub with small white or yellow flowers that have a very sweet smell, or the scent taken from those flowers
core_image: 夏夜窗前一大片白色小花，香气顺风一阵阵涌进屋子
scene: 夏夜，院墙边的白色小花开了，风一吹，整个巷子都是清甜的香气。On a summer night the jasmine along the wall opened, and the whole lane smelled of it.
sceneCN: 这里 jasmine 是「茉莉；茉莉花」（第 1 个义项：开白色小花、香气浓郁的攀援灌木）；句意：夏夜里墙边的茉莉开了，整条巷子都弥漫着它的香气。

pos.zh: 茉莉；茉莉花（植物或花朵）
茉莉香；茉莉花香型的香味（如茶与香水中的茉莉味）

collocations.zh: 夜来香（夜间开花、香气浓的白花灌木）

forms.label: 指植物本身时的不可数用法

derivatives.zh: jasmine 与 scented 组成的复合形容词，义为「带茉莉花香的」
jasmine 的异体拼写，多见于旧文献与植物名，也指素馨属植物  （注：有时专指 Gelsemium 属的有毒断肠草，须看语境）
由茉莉属的拉丁属名 Jasminum 加形容词后缀 -aceous（属于……科的）构成，义为「茉莉属的、茉莉科的」

senses.title: The climbing shrub
senses.definition: a climbing shrub of the olive family with small white or yellow fragrant flowers
senses.definitionCN: 橄榄科的一类攀援灌木，开小而香的白色或黄色花
senses.example: Jasmine climbs happily over a sunny wall.
senses.exampleCN: 茉莉喜欢沿着向阳的墙攀爬。
senses.why: The word was borrowed as a plant name from Persian through Arabic, and the plant sense is its first and oldest meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是经阿拉伯语从波斯语借入的植物名，植物义是它最古老、最基础的含义。

senses.title: The fragrant flowers
senses.definition: the small, sweet-smelling flowers of this plant, often picked for tea or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物小而香的花，常被采来泡茶或装饰
senses.example: She floated a few jasmine flowers in the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 她在杯里放了几朵茉莉花。
senses.why: The flower is the reason people grow the plant, so the plant name came to name its blossoms as a countable object.
senses.whyCN: 花是人们栽种茉莉的理由，于是植物名也顺着转指一朵朵可数的小花。

senses.title: The sweet scent
senses.definition: the heavy, sweet smell of jasmine, or a perfume or flavouring made to smell like it
senses.definitionCN: 茉莉浓郁甜美的气味，也指模仿这种气味的香精或味道
senses.example: The night air was heavy with jasmine.
senses.exampleCN: 夜色里的空气弥漫着浓郁的茉莉香。
