senses.why: Because the flower is prized above all for its smell, the name slides from the flower to the scent it leaves in the air.
senses.whyCN: 因为茉莉最出名的就是香气，名字便从花本身滑到花香上，指那股留在空气里的气味。

intro.en: Jasmine travelled from Persia through Arabic and the Mediterranean trading routes into English, bringing both the plant and its name.
intro.cn: jasmine 从波斯经阿拉伯语与地中海商路传入英语，连同植物和名字一起传了过来。

items.en: A word reconstructed as yasmin names the jasmine plant.
items.cn: 重构形式 yasmin 指茉莉属植物，这是该词的波斯语源头。

items.en: Arabic yasmin keeps the plant name and passes it westward.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 yasmin 保留植物名，并把它向西传播。

items.en: Latin texts record forms such as jessamine and jasminum.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁文献记下 jessamine、jasminum 等形式。

items.en: French jessemin or jasmin carries the word into western Europe.
items.cn: 法语的 jessemin 或 jasmin 把词带入西欧。

items.en: English adopts jasmine for the fragrant shrub.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语采用 jasmine 指这种香花灌木。

items.en: The modern sense widens to the perfume, the tea and the rice.
items.cn: 现代义扩展到茉莉香型、花茶和香米等。

note.en: Jasmine is a plant name first, so it sits close to other flowers in form and to anything sweet-smelling in meaning.
note.cn: jasmine 首先是植物名，形式上与其它花卉词相近，意义上与各种芳香的词相邻。

entries.definition: an old spelling of jasmine
entries.definitionCN: jasmine 的旧拼写，多见于旧文献，也指几种有毒的断肠草

entries.definition: blue or purple stones called jacinth
entries.definitionCN: 一种蓝紫色宝石的复数；与 jasmine 只是读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the French form of the plant name
entries.definitionCN: 法语中茉莉的拼法，比英语少一个 e 之外的差异，是同源借词

entries.definition: green tea scented with jasmine flowers
entries.definitionCN: 用茉莉花窨制的绿茶，即茉莉花茶

entries.definition: an evergreen shrub with showy flowers
a shrub with fragrant purple flowers
entries.definitionCN: 薰衣草，开紫色香花的灌木

normalIntro.en: Jasmine is the Persian plant name that came west by sea, and its smell gave English a second and third word.
normalIntro.cn: jasmine 是循海路西传的波斯植物名，它的香气又让英语长出了第二、第三层意思。

normal.en: Jasmine tea is green tea scented with fresh jasmine flowers.
normal.cn: jasmine tea 是用新鲜茉莉花窨制的绿茶。

normal.en: Jasmine rice has a soft, flowery smell and turns fluffy when cooked.
normal.cn: jasmine rice 即茉莉香米，有淡淡的花香，煮熟后松软蓬松。

normal.en: At night, jasmine opens and its scent travels far.
normal.cn: 夜里茉莉开得最盛，香气能飘得很远。

normal.en: The -ne ending marks the old spelling, later simplified to plain jasm-in patterns.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ne 是老式拼写的痕迹，后来拼写逐渐简化成 jasm- 的样子。

normal.en: Compare lavender: both plant names stand for the scent as much as the plant.
normal.cn: 对比 lavender：两者都既是植物名，也直接代表那种香气。

abstract.en: Picture a pergola dripping with white stars of small flowers.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花架，垂满像白色小星星一样的花。

abstract.en: Hold a porcelain cup and watch a tiny white flower unfurl in hot water.
abstract.cn: 手握一只瓷杯，看着一朵小白花在热水里慢慢舒展。

abstract.en: Close your eyes and let one breath of garden fill the whole room.
abstract.cn: 闭上眼，让呼吸到的一口花园香气充满整个房间。

examples.en: The jasmine by the window perfumes the whole bedroom at night.
examples.cn: 窗边的茉莉在夜里把整间卧室熏得清香。

examples.en: She ordered a pot of jasmine tea with the dim sum.
examples.cn: 她点了点心时配一壶茉莉花茶。

examples.en: Jasmine grows well along a sunny wall but dislikes frost.
examples.cn: 茉莉在向阳的墙边长得好，却怕霜冻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎斯敏」——听起来像一朵扎扎实实的小白花，香气直往鼻子里钻；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 波斯语 yasmin（茉莉属植物）→ 阿拉伯语 yasmin → 中世纪拉丁语形式与法语 jasmin、jessemin → 十六世纪英语 jasmine；核心义「香白小花攀着墙开」。

sensesIntro.en: Jasmine names the plant first, then its small flowers, and finally the sweet scent those flowers leave behind.
sensesIntro.cn: jasmine 先指这种植物，再指它的小花，最后指花朵留下的那股甜香。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of white summer flowers sending its scent indoors.
core.cn: 核心意象：一墙夏夜里的小白花，把香气送进屋里。

branches.en: The shrub itself is the botanical sense.
branches.cn: 灌木本身是植物学义项。

branches.en: The blossoms picked for tea and decoration are the flower sense.
branches.cn: 采来泡茶和装饰的花朵是花义项。

branches.en: The lingering smell and its perfume copies are the scent sense.
branches.cn: 久久不散的气味及仿制的香精是香气义项。

branches.en: The plant is grown precisely because its flowers are worth picking.
branches.cn: 人们栽种茉莉，正是为了摘下它的花。

branches.en: Flowers turn into fragrance, and fragrance turns into tea and rice.
branches.cn: 花变成香气，香气又变成花茶与香米。

intro.en: Jasmine is a borrowed plant name with little English word-building, so most related forms are compounds or older spellings.
intro.cn: jasmine 是借来的植物名，英语构词不多，相关词形多是复合词或旧拼写。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin wrote the plant as jasminum or jessamine, keeping the Arabic shape of the name.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这种植物写作 jasminum 或 jessamine，保留了阿拉伯语形式。

items.example: Jasmine is the standard modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: jasmine 是现代标准拼写。

items.example: Old texts write jessamine for the flower.
items.exampleCN: 旧文献把这种花写作 jessamine。

items.example: Jasminum is also the botanical genus name.
items.exampleCN: Jasminum 同时也是植物学的属名。

items.example: The suffix -scented forms jasmine-scented.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -scented 构成 jasmine-scented。

items.example: A jasmine-scented candle filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 一支茉莉香气的蜡烛充满了大厅。

items.example: Jasmine tea is the most famous use of the flower.
items.exampleCN: 茉莉花茶是这种花最出名的用途。

items.example: Jasmine rice took the name from its smell.
items.exampleCN: 茉莉香米的名字取自它的香味。

items.example: French jessemin carries the word westward.
items.exampleCN: 法语 jessemin 把词向西传播。

items.example: Night jasmine opens after dusk.
items.exampleCN: 夜来香在黄昏后开放。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 茉莉（来自阿拉伯语形式的拼法）

definition_zh: 水母；海蜇；软弱无能的人；优柔寡断的人
definition_en: a soft, umbrella-shaped sea animal with a clear body and long stinging tentacles, or a weak person who gives in easily
core_image: 一只半透明的伞状生物在海水中一张一合，拖着长长的触手缓缓漂过
scene: 退潮后，沙滩边浮着一只半透明的小伞，触手还在轻轻摆动，孩子伸手去碰，被大人一把拉住。After the tide went out, a small clear jellyfish was floating by the sand, its tentacles still swaying, and a child reached out until an adult pulled the hand back.
sceneCN: 这里 jellyfish 是「水母」（第 1 个义项：身体透明柔软、触手带刺的海生动物）；句意：退潮后沙滩边漂着一只小小的透明水母，触手还在摆动，孩子伸手去碰，被大人一把拉回。

pos.zh: 软弱的人；没骨气的人；优柔寡断者（比喻用法）

collocations.zh: 水母季；适合下水但水母多的时节

derivatives.zh: jellyfish 的前半部分，义为「果冻；胶状物」，说明它的身体像一团透明胶质
jellyfish 的后半部分，义为「鱼」，是个通俗归类词，并非水母的真正分类
jellyfish 的历史异体拼写，见于较早的英语文献与方言
jelly 的复数，也常被用来指水母这一类胶质生物，是水母的通俗说法

senses.title: The sea animal
senses.definition: a soft-bodied, umbrella-shaped sea animal with a clear jellylike body and stinging tentacles
senses.definitionCN: 一种身体柔软、呈伞状的海洋动物，身体透明如果冻，触手带刺
senses.example: A jellyfish drifted past the boat, pulsing slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 一只水母缓缓从船边漂过，身体一收一放。
senses.why: The name is a plain English compound of jelly and fish, describing a creature that looks like a blob of jelly in the sea.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字是英语自造的复合词，由 jelly（果冻）和 fish（鱼）拼成，形容一种在海里像团果冻的「鱼」。

senses.title: Swimmers hurt by them
senses.definition: a swimming hazard or injury caused by the stings of these animals in the water
senses.definitionCN: 在水中因水母蜇刺而造成的危险或伤口
senses.example: Two swimmers were treated for jellyfish stings on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 两名游泳者在海滩上接受了水母蜇伤的处理。
senses.why: Because the animal is common in warm waters and its stings are painful, the name also stands for the danger itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为水母在温水海域很常见、蜇人又疼，这个名字也转指这种危险本身。

senses.title: A weak, spineless person
senses.titleCN: 软弱无能的人；没骨气的人
senses.definition: an informal, critical term for someone with no backbone who gives in easily
senses.definitionCN: 口语中带贬义的称呼，指没有骨气、轻易让步的人
senses.example: Stop acting like a jellyfish and stand up for your team.
senses.exampleCN: 别像个没骨头的人，替你团队站出来说话。
senses.why: A jellyfish has no bones and only drifts with the current, so the image becomes a picture of a person without a spine.
senses.whyCN: 水母没有骨头，只会随水流漂，于是这个形象变成了「没有脊梁骨的人」的比喻。

intro.en: Jellyfish is not a borrowing but a plain English compound, built from two everyday words.
intro.cn: jellyfish 不是借词，而是用两个日常词拼成的英语复合词。

items.en: Jelly comes from Old French gelée, a jelly or frosty congealed mass.
items.cn: jelly 来自古法语 gelée，意为凝胶、冻住的胶状物。

items.en: Fish long served as a loose word for almost any water creature.
items.cn: fish 长期宽松地指几乎任何水生生物。

items.en: Mariners begin describing sea animals as jellyfish for their transparent jellylike bodies.
items.cn: 十六世纪航海者因其透明胶质身体，开始把这类海生生物称作 jellyfish。

items.en: The compound is fixed in natural history writing for the medusa group.
items.cn: 十八世纪博物学写作中，该复合词固定指水母类。

items.en: The figurative sense of a spineless person develops in informal speech and writing.
items.cn: 十九世纪口语与书信中发展出「没骨气的人」的比喻义。

items.en: Modern science notes that a jellyfish is not a fish, yet the everyday name remains.
items.cn: 现代科学指出水母并不是鱼，但日常叫法一直保留。

note.en: Jellyfish is a compound built on jelly, close in form to jelly and in meaning to other soft-sea and soft-person words.
note.cn: jellyfish 是以 jelly 为基础构成的复合词，形式上与 jelly 相近，意义上与各种软体海生动物以及软弱之人的说法相邻。

entries.definition: a soft, transparent food holding its shape
entries.definitionCN: 果冻；胶状物，是 jellyfish 的前半部分

entries.definition: an animal that lives and breathes in water
entries.definitionCN: 鱼，是 jellyfish 的后半部分，此处只是通俗归类

entries.definition: having the texture of jelly
entries.definitionCN: 像果冻一样的，常用来形容水母的身体

entries.definition: the free-swimming bell stage of a jellyfish
entries.definitionCN: 水母的伞状自由游泳阶段，科学用语

entries.definition: a soft sea animal with tentacles around a mouth
entries.definitionCN: 海葵，与水母同属刺胞动物

entries.definition: weak and easily pushed around
entries.definitionCN: 没骨气的、软弱的，与比喻义对应

normalIntro.en: Jellyfish wears its two halves on the outside: jelly plus fish, a jelly-like creature wrongly filed under fish.
normalIntro.cn: jellyfish 把两半都写在脸上：jelly 加 fish，一个像果冻的生物被误归到鱼里。

normal.en: A jellyfish sting leaves a red, stinging mark on the skin.
normal.cn: 被水母蜇一下，皮肤上会留下一道又红又疼的痕迹。

normal.en: A jellyfish bloom means huge numbers of them crowding the shore.
normal.cn: jellyfish bloom 指大量水母挤在近岸。

normal.en: Jellyfish tentacles trail behind the bell like thin strings.
normal.cn: 水母的触手像细线一样拖在伞体后面。

normal.en: The plural can be plain jellyfish, just as with fish.
normal.cn: 它的复数和 fish 一样，可以仍然写作 jellyfish。

normal.en: Compare medusa: medusa is the scientific name, jellyfish the everyday word.
normal.cn: 对比 medusa：medusa 是科学称谓，jellyfish 是日常说法。

abstract.en: Picture a parachute of clear jelly opening and closing under the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶透明果冻做的降落伞在水下开开合合。

abstract.en: See a pale cup with long threads of string trailing from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只浅色小杯，拖着长长的线一样的触手。

abstract.en: Think of a figure with no bones, drifting wherever the current goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有骨头的影子，顺着水流漂向哪里就是哪里。

examples.en: Warm seas can bring jellyfish blooms that close beaches for days.
examples.cn: 温暖的海水会造成水母暴发，导致海滩关闭好几天。

examples.en: She was stung by a jellyfish while swimming off the coast.
examples.cn: 她在近海游泳时被水母蜇了。

examples.en: The team needed a leader, not another jellyfish who agreed with everyone.
examples.cn: 这个团队需要一位领导者，而不是又一个谁说的话都点头的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「结粒鱼」——像一团结住的透明胶粒在水里漂，被当成鱼，其实是水母；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语复合词：jelly（果冻，源自拉丁语 gelare「冻结」→ 古法语 gelée）+ fish（古英语 fisc，泛指水中生物）；核心义「像果冻一样软的海洋生物」。

sensesIntro.en: Jellyfish names the animal, then the sting it causes, and finally, by its lack of bones, a spineless person.
sensesIntro.cn: jellyfish 先指这种动物，再指它造成的蜇伤，最后借它没有骨头这一点转指没骨气的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear jelly umbrella pulsing through the sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶透明的果冻伞在海里一张一合地穿行。

branches.en: The umbrella-shaped sea animal is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 伞状海洋动物是字面义项。

branches.en: The pain and danger of its stings are the swimming sense.
branches.cn: 它蜇刺带来的疼痛与危险是游泳场景义项。

branches.en: A person without a backbone is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 没有脊梁骨的人是比喻义项。

branches.en: The animal and its stings arrive together whenever it drifts too close.
branches.cn: 这种动物只要漂得太近，本尊和蜇伤就一起出现。

branches.en: Its soft body and drifting motion supply the picture of weakness.
branches.cn: 它柔软的身体和随波漂动，提供了软弱的画面。

intro.en: Jellyfish is a home-grown compound, and most related forms are built from its two halves or from jelly.
intro.cn: jellyfish 是英语土生复合词，相关词形多由它的两半或 jelly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root sits in jelly: gelare, to freeze or congeal, though the compound itself came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁根源在 jelly 里：gelare 意为冻结、凝结，不过复合词本身是经法语传来的。

items.example: The body of a jellyfish is mostly jelly.
items.exampleCN: 水母的身体大部分是胶质。

items.example: Gelare lies behind gelée and jelly.
items.exampleCN: gelare 是 gelée 与 jelly 的词根。

items.example: Fish in the broad sense covers many sea creatures.
items.exampleCN: 广义的 fish 涵盖许多海洋生物。

items.example: The suffix -like forms jellylike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 jellylike。

items.example: Jellylike tissue makes up much of the animal.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物大部分是像果冻一样的组织。

items.example: Jellied eels are a London dish.
items.exampleCN: 鳗鱼冻是一道伦敦菜。

items.example: Jellyfish joins a food word to a fish word.
items.exampleCN: jellyfish 把一个食物词和一个鱼字拼在一起。

items.meaning: the swimming stage of the animal
items.example: Medusa is the technical label for the jellyfish bell.
items.exampleCN: medusa 是水母伞体阶段的技术名称。

items.meaning: used in names of sea creatures
items.meaningCN: 构成海生动物名称的复合成分
items.example: The element -fish also appears in shellfish.
items.exampleCN: 复合成分 -fish 也出现在 shellfish 里。

definition_zh: 危及；损害；使处于危险中
definition_en: to put something valuable or someone in danger of being harmed or lost
core_image: 一盘棋下到一半，双方胜负未定，一步走错就满盘皆输
scene: 预算被大幅削减，整个研究项目随时可能被叫停。The funding cut could jeopardise the whole research project.
sceneCN: 这里 jeopardise 是「危及」（第 2 个义项：使计划或项目面临失败的风险）；句意：削减经费可能危及整个研究项目。

pos.zh: 危及；损害；使处于危险中

derivatives.zh: 由中古英语 jeu parti 演化而来的名词，义为「危险；危难」
基础名词加 -ous 后缀构成的书面用语，义为「危险的」
动词加 -ing 后缀名物化，义为「危及这一行为」

senses.title: To endanger someone
senses.definition: to put a person in danger of harm, injury, or loss
senses.definitionCN: 使人面临受到伤害、损伤或损失的危险
senses.example: The leaky gas pipe jeopardised the workers.
senses.exampleCN: 漏气的煤气管道使工人们陷入了危险。
senses.why: The root image is a game with an even chance, so to jeopardise someone is to leave their safety hanging on a doubtful move.
senses.whyCN: 词根意象是胜负未定的棋局，所以危及某人就是把他的安危押在一个不确定的招法上。

senses.title: To put a plan or project at risk
senses.titleCN: 使计划或项目面临失败风险
senses.definition: to threaten the success of a plan, project, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 威胁到计划、项目或安排的成败
senses.example: A single strike could jeopardise the whole schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 一次罢工会危及整个工期。
senses.why: Once the game image is extended to plans, any risk to the finished result becomes a threat to the whole project.
senses.whyCN: 棋局意象延伸到计划之后，对最终结果的风险就成了对整个项目的威胁。

senses.title: To harm a relationship or reputation
senses.definition: to damage trust, a relationship, or a good name
senses.definitionCN: 损害信任、关系或良好的名声
senses.example: The careless remark jeopardised the partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 那句轻率的话损害了合作关系。
senses.why: The same betting logic applies to intangible goods such as trust, which can be lost in one bad move.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「押注」逻辑也适用于信任这类无形之物，一步走错就可能全部输掉。

senses.title: To imperil health or safety
senses.definition: to make health, safety, or life less secure
senses.definitionCN: 使健康、安全或生命变得更不安全
senses.example: Cutting the water supply jeopardises public health.
senses.exampleCN: 切断供水会危及公共卫生。
senses.why: When the thing at stake is health, the chance element of the game turns into a simple risk of harm.
senses.whyCN: 当赌注换成健康时，棋局里的偶然性就变成了实实在在的伤害风险。

senses.title: To threaten something rare or valuable
senses.definition: to put something rare, such as a species or a landscape, in danger of disappearing
senses.definitionCN: 使物种、景观等稀有之物面临消失的危险
senses.example: Tourism has jeopardised the nesting birds.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业已经威胁到了筑巢的鸟类。
senses.why: What can be lost under the open game image includes not only people but also things that cannot be replaced.
senses.whyCN: 在「胜负未定」的意象下可能输掉的不只是人，还包括无法替代的珍稀之物。

senses.title: To risk losing an advantage
senses.definition: to take a course of action that may cost an existing advantage
senses.definitionCN: 采取可能让已有优势付诸东流的做法
senses.example: He refused to jeopardise his lead on the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一圈拒绝冒丢掉领先优势的风险。
senses.why: In a game of uncertain outcome, a player who gambles may keep everything or throw away a lead, and the verb names that gamble.
senses.whyCN: 胜负未定的棋局里，敢赌的一方要么全赢、要么丢掉领先，动词所指的正是这一赌注。

senses.title: To put peace or stability in doubt
senses.definition: to make peace, order, or stability uncertain
senses.definitionCN: 使和平、秩序或稳定变得不确定
senses.example: Border disputes jeopardise the peace talks.
senses.exampleCN: 边界争端使和谈变得岌岌可危。
senses.why: Political language borrows the game image for collective goods that hang on a single risky decision.
senses.whyCN: 政治话语借用了棋局意象，用来指那些系于一次冒险决定的集体利益。

senses.title: To threaten (the American spelling)
senses.definition: same sense, spelled with z in American English
senses.definitionCN: 同一词义，在美式英语中拼作 z 结尾
senses.example: Unsafe wiring could jeopardize the building.
senses.exampleCN: 不安全的电线可能危及整栋楼。
senses.why: American and British spelling split only at the final letter, while the game image behind the word stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 美式拼写只在词尾字母上与英式不同，词后那幅「棋局」意象完全一样。

intro.en: Jeopardy comes from Old French jeu parti, a divided or even game, in which the fairest move keeps the chance of loss alive.
intro.cn: jeopardy 来自古法语 jeu parti，本义是「胜负未分的对局」，其中双方机会均衡，输的可能始终存在。

items.en: Jeu parti means a divided game, a match whose outcome is still open.
items.cn: jeu parti 意为被均分的对局，即胜负尚未确定的比赛。

items.en: In the chess treatise of around 1300 the phrase also names a doubtful or risky position.
items.cn: 约一千三百年的象棋论著中，这个词组也指可疑、有风险的局面。

items.en: English borrows the phrase as jeopardie around the fourteenth century, meaning a chance of loss.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪前后借入这一词组，写作 jeopardie，意为「蒙受损失的可能」。

items.en: The noun loses its chess flavour and settles on the meaning of danger.
items.cn: 名词逐渐褪去棋局色彩，固定为「危险」之义。

items.en: The verb appears as jeopardise in the nineteenth century, formed from the noun.
items.cn: 动词 jeopardise 出现于十九世纪，由名词派生而成。

items.en: The -ise and -ize spellings split between Britain and America.
items.cn: 现代英语中，-ise 与 -ize 两种拼写在英、美两地分道扬镳。

note.en: Jeopardise belongs to the gamble family around jeopardy, and sits close to the plain danger words.
note.cn: jeopardise 属于 jeopardy 的「押注」词族，并与普通的「危险」类词义相邻。

entries.definition: danger of loss or harm
entries.definitionCN: 危险的境地；蒙受损失的可能

entries.definition: full of danger
to put in danger
to put someone or something in danger
to be likely to harm something
to weaken something gradually

normalIntro.en: Jeopardise keeps the picture of an even game: your safe position is only one shaky move from being lost.
normalIntro.cn: jeopardise 保留了对局均势的画面：你安全的位置离失去只差一个不稳的招法。

normal.en: Jeopardy means danger, so to jeopardise is to place in danger.
normal.cn: jeopardy 是危险，jeopardise 就是使之陷入危险。

normal.en: The British spelling ends in -ise, the American in -ize.
normal.cn: 英式拼写以 -ise 结尾，美式拼写以 -ize 结尾。

normal.en: The verb is transitive and takes the thing at risk as its object.
normal.cn: 这是及物动词，宾语正是处于危险中的那个事物。

normal.en: The passive form is common: jobs may be jeopardised by a policy.
normal.cn: 被动式很常见：「jobs may be jeopardised by a policy」即岗位可能因某项政策受到威胁。

normal.en: Compare endanger: endanger is neutral and factual, jeopardise adds a note of gamble and loss.
normal.cn: 对比 endanger：endanger 中性客观，jeopardise 多了一层「押上赌注、可能输掉」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a worker standing on a cracked platform above a drop.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人站在裂了缝的高台边上，脚下是深坑。

abstract.en: Picture a chessboard where one careless move can overturn the whole game.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘棋，一步不慎就可能翻盘。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on paper that a single spill can ruin.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写在纸上的名字，一杯水打翻就能毁掉。

examples.en: Rising sea levels jeopardise coastal villages.
examples.cn: 海平面上升危及沿海村庄。

examples.en: He would never jeopardise his career for a quick gain.
examples.cn: 他绝不会为了短期利益而危及自己的事业。

examples.en: The deadline must not be jeopardised by poor planning.
examples.cn: 不能因规划不当而危及最后期限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「节拍打死」——棋局打到节拍乱、打死结，胜负未定，正是「危及」之时；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 jeu parti（胜负未分的对局）→ 中古英语 jeopardie（蒙受损失的可能）→ 英语 jeopardy（危险）→ jeopardise（使陷入危险），核心义「把安危押在一局未定的棋上」。

sensesIntro.en: Jeopardise starts with a person left in danger, widens to plans, relationships, health, rare things and advantages, and finally notes the spelling split.
sensesIntro.cn: jeopardise 先指使人陷入险境，再扩展到计划、关系、健康、珍稀事物与已有优势，最后记录拼写差异。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess game with an even chance, lost by one wrong move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘胜负未定的棋，一步走错便满盘皆输。

branches.en: A person in physical danger is the plainest reading.
branches.cn: 人身处于险境是最朴素的读法。

branches.en: A project at risk extends the game to plans.
branches.cn: 项目面临失败，是把棋局延伸到计划上。

branches.en: Relations, reputations, peace, and order are collective stakes.
branches.cn: 关系、声誉、和平与秩序都是集体层面的赌注。

branches.en: Health and rare species can be lost like a stake on the board.
branches.cn: 健康与珍稀物种也像棋盘上的赌注一样可能被输掉。

branches.en: A gamble for advantage and the American spelling close the circle.
branches.cn: 为优势而冒险与美式拼写为这一词义圈收尾。

intro.en: Jeopardise is built on the noun jeopardy plus the verb suffix -ise, with the American -ize close behind.
intro.cn: jeopardise 由名词 jeopardy 加动词后缀 -ise 构成，美式拼写沿用 -ize。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family here: the word is French jeu parti turned into an English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁同族词：它由法语 jeu parti 演变为英语名词，再派生出动词。

items.example: The crew was in jeopardy during the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨中船员们身处险境。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把名词变成动词。

items.example: Jeopardise is the standard British form.
items.exampleCN: jeopardise 是英式标准拼写。

items.example: The suffix -ize gives the American form.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成美式拼写。

items.example: Jeopardised appears in passive constructions.
items.exampleCN: jeopardised 常见于被动结构。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms jeopardous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 jeopardous。

items.example: Jeopardous is a rare literary word.
items.exampleCN: jeopardous 是罕见的书面词。

items.example: The suffix -ing names the act of jeopardising.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 表示危及这一行为。

items.meaning: the act of putting at risk
items.example: Jeopardising the plan was a costly error.
items.exampleCN: 危及计划是个代价高昂的错误。

definition_zh: 猛拉；急扯；猛地一动；笨蛋； jerk 肉
definition_en: to pull or move something suddenly and sharply, or a sudden sharp movement
core_image: 被人猛地一扯，身子向前一顿，随即弹回原处
scene: 绳子被猛地一扯，桶里的水泼了出来。He gave the rope a jerk and the bucket tipped over.
sceneCN: 这里 jerk 是「猛一拉」（第 1 个义项：突然而短暂的一扯）；句意：他猛地一拉绳子，桶就翻了。

collocations.zh: 膝跳反应；条件反射式的反应
一顿一顿地；断断续续地

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -y 后缀构成的形容词，义为「急促而不平稳的」
jerky 加 -ly 后缀构成的副词，义为「一顿一顿地」
jerky 加 -ness 后缀构成的名词，义为「突然的颠动」

senses.title: A sudden sharp pull
senses.definition: a sudden, quick, sharp pull on something
senses.definitionCN: 突然、快速而有力地一拉扯动某物
senses.example: She gave the drawer a hard jerk.
senses.exampleCN: 她猛地把抽屉一拉。
senses.why: The word imitates a short, snappy movement, and a sharp pull is the most direct picture of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿的是短促有力的动作，而猛地一拉正是这幅画面最直接的呈现。

senses.title: To pull suddenly
senses.definition: to move or pull something with a sudden quick movement
senses.definitionCN: 用突然而快速的动作拉动或移动某物
senses.example: He jerked the cord to start the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛地一拉绳索启动引擎。
senses.why: The noun sense turns into a verb once the same sharp movement is performed on an object.
senses.whyCN: 把那一记短促的动作施加到某个物体上，名词义就自然转成了动词。

senses.title: A sudden uncontrolled movement
senses.definition: a short, quick movement of the body that is not fully controlled
senses.definitionCN: 身体不完全受控的短促动作
senses.example: His hand gave a nervous jerk.
senses.exampleCN: 他的手紧张地抽动了一下。
senses.why: When the movement happens to a body rather than an object, the same snap reads as a twitch or jolt.
senses.whyCN: 当这个短促动作发生在身体上而非物体上时，同样的「一顿」就变成了抽搐或颤动。

senses.title: A jolt while riding
senses.definition: a bumpy, uneven movement of a vehicle or a rider
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或乘骑者不平稳、一顿一顿的运动
senses.example: The old bus moved forward in jerks.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧巴士一顿一顿地向前开。
senses.why: Repeated small streaks of motion add up to a jerky ride, the same image stretched over time and space.
senses.whyCN: 一个个短促的动作叠加起来，就成了颠簸的行进，还是同一个意象在时间和空间上的拉长。

senses.title: To throw with a sharp motion
senses.definition: to throw or fling something with a quick, snappy movement
senses.definitionCN: 用短促有力的动作抛掷某物
senses.example: She jerked the ball into the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 她手腕猛地一抖，把球抛进了篮筐。
senses.why: A throw is only a pull released, so the wrist snap behind a quick throw keeps the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 抛掷不过是拉拽的松手瞬间，快速出手时手腕那一抖仍然沿用原来的画面。

senses.title: A foolish or rude person
senses.definition: an offensive word for someone who is stupid or behaves badly
senses.definitionCN: 指愚蠢或举止恶劣者的冒犯性说法
senses.example: He behaved like a real jerk at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在派对上表现得活像个混蛋。
senses.why: In American slang the word shifted from a physical jolt to a person whose character gives others a jolt of irritation.
senses.whyCN: 在美式俚语里，这个词从身体上的「一顿」转指其为人给他人带来的那股恼人冲击。

senses.title: To cure meat with spice
senses.definition: to preserve meat by rubbing it with spices and drying it
senses.definitionCN: 用香料揉搓并晾干来保存肉类
senses.example: They jerked the venison over a slow fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把鹿肉用慢火熏制保存。
senses.why: This sense comes through Spanish charqui from a Quechua word, and only its spelling resembles the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项经西班牙语 charqui 来自克丘亚语，只是拼写与英语动词相像而已。

senses.title: A sharp physical shock
senses.definition: a sudden hard movement or shock, as in a sudden stop
senses.definitionCN: 行进中突然的剧烈震动，如急刹车时的一顿
senses.example: The car came to a halt with a jerk.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车猛地一顿停了下来。
senses.why: A sudden stop is a sudden change of speed, the clearest abstract echo of the short sharp movement.
senses.whyCN: 急停就是速度的骤然改变，是这种短促动作最清楚的抽象回响。

intro.en: Jerk is probably imitative in origin, a word formed to echo the sound and snap of a quick movement; the deep root is uncertain.
intro.cn: jerk 一般认为源于拟声造词，用来模仿快速动作的声音与顿挫；更早的词根来源不确定。

items.en: The word is first recorded in English in the sixteenth century with the sense of a sharp stroke.
items.cn: 该词十六世纪首次见于英语文献，义为「一记猛击」。

items.en: Meat jerking, the spiced cure, arrives separately through Spanish charqui.
items.cn: 肉类的 jerk 腌渍送义则是另一路，经西班牙语 charqui 传入。

items.en: The Quechua word charqui means dried meat and gives the meat sense through Spanish.
items.cn: 克丘亚语 charqui 意为干肉，经西班牙语演变为这一腌肉义项。

items.en: The noun and verb settle on the sudden pull and sudden movement meanings.
items.cn: 十八世纪，名词与动词都稳定在「猛然一拉」与「猛地一动」上。

items.en: In the twentieth century the slang sense of a contemptible person becomes common.
items.cn: 二十世纪，辱骂性的「讨厌鬼」这一俚语义开始流行。

items.en: The knee-jerk image enters politics as a phrase for an unthinking reaction.
items.cn: 膝跳的画面进入政治话语，用来指不假思索的反应。

note.en: Jerk is a snappy movement word, close to its own family and to the general verbs of pulling and nodding.
note.cn: jerk 表示短促有力的动作，与其词族以及笼统的「拉」「点」类动词相邻。

entries.definition: moving with sudden stops and starts
in a jerky way
the quality of being jerky
to pull something hard and suddenly
a quick small movement of a body part
to pull hard, often repeatedly

normalIntro.en: Jerk is the sound and feel of a snap: one short, hard movement that stops as suddenly as it starts.
normalIntro.cn: jerk 是「一顿」的声音与手感：短促有力的一动，起得急、停得也急。

normal.en: Add -y and jerk becomes jerky, an adjective for an uneven movement.
normal.cn: 加上 -y 就得到 jerky，表示动作不平稳。

normal.en: The phrase knee-jerk reaction pictures the leg shooting forward without thought.
normal.cn: 「knee-jerk reaction」描绘的是小腿不假思索地弹出去。

normal.en: As a noun jerk can name the pull itself or the person who is a nuisance.
normal.cn: 作名词时，jerk 既可指那一拉，也可指令人讨厌的人。

normal.en: The verb is regular: jerks, jerked, jerking.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：jerks、jerked、jerking。

normal.en: Compare yank: yank is informal and stresses force, jerk stresses suddenness.
normal.cn: 对比 yank：yank 口语化、强调用劲，jerk 强调突然。

abstract.en: Picture a dog at the end of a leash when it spots a cat.
abstract.cn: 想象狗在牵引绳尽头看见猫的那一下猛冲。

abstract.en: Picture a head whipping round at the sound of its name.
abstract.cn: 想象听见有人叫自己名字时，脑袋猛地一转。

abstract.en: Picture an old lift that stops with a hard bump.
abstract.cn: 想象一部老电梯停下时重重一顿。

examples.en: The driver jerked the wheel to avoid the dog.
examples.cn: 司机猛打方向盘躲开了那条狗。

examples.en: He woke with a jerk when the alarm rang.
examples.cn: 闹钟一响，他猛地惊醒。

examples.en: The train pulled away in a series of jerks.
examples.cn: 火车一顿一顿地开走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎克」——扎克被绳子一拽就跟着一窜，「扎」的一下一顿，正是 jerk 的猛拉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拟声起源（一般认为），模仿短促动作的声音与顿挫 → 英语 jerk（一记猛击 → 猛然一拉、猛地一动）；「腌肉」义另经西班牙语 charqui 来自克丘亚语，与本词并无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Jerk begins with a sharp pull and its verb, widens to twitches, jolts, throws and sudden shocks, adds the slang insult, and notes the separate meat sense.
sensesIntro.cn: jerk 从猛地一拉及其动词义出发，扩展到抽搐、颠簸、抛掷与猛然一震，再加入辱骂义，并交代另来源的腌肉义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one short hard yank that makes the body snap forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：猛地一扯，让身体向前一顿。

branches.en: The pull and the verb that performs it are the core pair.
branches.cn: 那一拉与实施它的动词是核心的一对。

branches.en: A twitch is the same snap happening inside a body.
branches.cn: 抽搐是同样的短促动作发生在身体内部。

branches.en: Rides and stops collect many small jolts into one jerk.
branches.cn: 颠簸与急停把许多小顿挫汇成一记猛顿。

branches.en: A quick fling keeps the wrist snap of the original pull.
branches.cn: 快速抛掷保留了原先拉拽时手腕的那一抖。

branches.en: The slang insult and the spiced meat show how other meanings attach to a word.
branches.cn: 俚语骂人与腌肉义展示了别的含义如何挂到同一个词上。

intro.en: Jerk is a short English word with a product family built on it: jerk, jerky, jerkily, jerkiness.
intro.cn: jerk 是简短的英语本族词，并衍生出 jerk、jerky、jerkily、jerkiness 这一族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin roots are involved here; only the meat sense travels through Spanish from Quechua.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁词根；只有腌肉义经西班牙语辗转来自克丘亚语。

items.meaning: a sudden sharp pull or movement
items.example: Jerk covers both the action and its name.
items.exampleCN: jerk 既是动作也是这个动作的名称。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -y forms jerky.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 jerky。

items.example: Jerky describes uneven motion.
items.exampleCN: jerky 描述不平稳的动作。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms jerkily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 jerkily。

items.example: The car moved jerkily over the stones.
items.exampleCN: 汽车在石路上颠簸前行。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms jerkiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 jerkiness。

items.example: Jerkiness makes the footage hard to watch.
items.exampleCN: 画面颠簸让人难以观看。

items.meaningCN: 条件反射式的；不假思索的
items.example: Knee-jerk is used mostly in the phrase knee-jerk reaction.
items.exampleCN: knee-jerk 多用于膝跳反应这一固定说法。

items.meaning: small and unimportant, of a town
items.example: Jerkwater town is a dated American phrase.
items.exampleCN: jerkwater town 是过时的美式说法。

definition_zh: 推挤；撞；争抢；争夺；与……竞争
definition_en: to push, bump, or shove against someone in a crowd, or to struggle for a position
core_image: 早高峰的地铁里，人群挤成一团，你推我撞，谁也站不稳
scene: 早高峰的车厢里，人群推来撞去，有人连伞都挤掉了。Commuters jostled one another as the doors opened.
sceneCN: 这里 jostle 是「推挤」（第 1 个义项：在人群中用身体互相推撞）；句意：车门一开，通勤的人们便互相推挤起来。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -ing 后缀名物化，义为「推挤；拥挤中的碰撞」
基础词加施事后缀 -er，义为「推挤他人的人」

senses.title: To push against people in a crowd
senses.definition: to push or bump against people roughly in a crowded place
senses.definitionCN: 在拥挤的地方用身体粗鲁地推撞他人
senses.example: The crowd jostled us toward the exit.
senses.exampleCN: 人群把我们挤向出口。
senses.why: In Latin, a iuxta, beside, and a joust, a knock, meet: bodies pressed close and striking each other is the core picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中「并排」与「冲撞」相遇：身体贴得很近并互相撞击，正是核心画面。

senses.title: To make your way by pushing
senses.definition: to move forward by pushing through a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 靠推挤穿过人群向前移动
senses.example: He jostled his way to the front of the queue.
senses.exampleCN: 他一路挤到了队伍最前面。
senses.why: Pushing against others also moves you somewhere, so the crowd press becomes a means of progress.
senses.whyCN: 推撞他人同时也在推动自己，所以人群的挤压也就成了一种前行的手段。

senses.title: To fight for a place or advantage
senses.definition: to compete with others for a position, share, or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 为位置、份额或优势与他人竞争
senses.example: Firms jostle for a share of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 各公司争抢市场份额。
senses.why: The physical scramble becomes a metaphor once the crowd is a market and the bodies are brands.
senses.whyCN: 当人群变成市场、身体变成品牌，身体上的推挤就化作了比喻。

senses.title: To struggle to get attention
senses.definition: to try hard to attract notice when many others are doing the same
senses.definitionCN: 在众人都想引人注目时努力争取注意
senses.example: The headlines jostle for attention every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早晨各条头条都在争抢注意力。
senses.why: Attention is a scarce space, so crowding around it feels like being pushed in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是稀缺的空间，围着它抢就仿佛在人群里被推挤。

senses.title: A bump in a crowd
senses.definition: a bump or push given to someone in a crowded place
senses.definitionCN: 在拥挤处对他人造成的一撞或一推
senses.example: He felt a jostle from behind on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 在楼梯上他感到背后被人撞了一下。
senses.why: The same event named by a verb can also be named by a noun when you need to point at one collision.
senses.whyCN: 动词所描述的事，在需要指认某一次碰撞时也可以用名词来称呼。

senses.title: To knock a thing aside
senses.definition: to knock or shake objects out of place by pushing past them
senses.definitionCN: 推挤经过时把物品撞歪或震落
senses.example: The busy waiter jostled the glasses on the tray.
senses.exampleCN: 忙碌的服务员把托盘上的杯子撞得东倒西歪。
senses.why: Things in a cramped space are jostled in exactly the same way people are.
senses.whyCN: 在狭小空间里，物品被挤得摇晃，与人群被挤是同一回事。

senses.title: To press against an idea
senses.definition: to put pressure on a belief, role, or position so that it seems less secure
senses.definitionCN: 对信念、角色或地位施加压力，使其显得不那么稳固
senses.example: Doubt jostled against his confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 疑虑不断动摇他的信心。
senses.why: Abstract things crowded together also press on one another, so an idea can be jostled like a body.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物挤在一起时也会相互施压，因此观点也能像身体一样被推挤。

senses.title: To push with the elbow
senses.definition: to shove someone with a shoulder or elbow to get past
senses.definitionCN: 用肩膀或手肘推撞他人以便通过
senses.example: An elbow jostled my arm on the escalator.
senses.exampleCN: 在自动扶梯上，有人用胳膊肘撞了我的手臂。
senses.why: The English noun joust steered the word toward the sturdier kind of shove, the one given by a shoulder or an elbow.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的名词 joust「冲撞」把词义引向了更结实的一推，即用肩或肘的碰撞。

intro.en: Jostle joins the Latin adverb iuxta, meaning beside, to a knock or joust, so the word pictures people pressed side by side and hitting each other.
intro.cn: jostle 把意为「旁边」的拉丁语副词 iuxta 与「撞击、冲撞」结合起来，描绘人们并排相贴、彼此撞击的画面。

items.en: Iuxta means beside or next to, the place word behind joust and jostle.
items.cn: iuxta 意为「旁边、紧挨着」，是 joust 与 jostle 背后的位置词。

items.en: Joster means to come together for a joust, the mounted clash of knights.
items.cn: joster 意为「聚集进行马上长矛比武」，即骑士骑马对冲。

items.en: English takes the tournament verb joust, knight against knight.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入比武动词 joust，指骑士与骑士相撞。

items.en: The frequentative jostle appears, first as a knock or shove, then as crowding in a press of people.
items.cn: 带有反复意味的 jostle 出现，先指一记推撞，后指在人群中被挤来挤去。

items.en: The word spreads from crowds and streets to business and politics.
items.cn: 这个词从人群与街道扩展到商业与政治。

items.en: Modern usage keeps both the bodily shove and the figurative scramble for advantage.
items.cn: 现代用法既保留了身体上的推撞，也保留了为争夺利益的角力。

note.en: Jostle is a crowded-space verb, near its own family and the ordinary verbs of pushing and shoving.
note.cn: jostle 是「拥挤空间」类动词，与其词族以及普通的「推、撞」动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of pushing against others
a person who pushes others aside
to fight on horseback with lances
to push something forcefully
to push past people with your elbows
entries.definitionCN: 用手肘推开他人挤过去

entries.definition: to get into a tight space with effort

normalIntro.en: Jostle keeps the old joust: side by side, bodies knock into one another until someone moves through.
normalIntro.cn: jostle 保留了古老的「比武」意味：并排相贴，身体互相撞击，直到有人挤过去。

normal.en: Jostle and joust share a root, and a joust is a clash; jostle keeps the clash and drops the horses.
normal.cn: jostle 与 joust 同根，joust 是冲撞；jostle 留着冲撞，丢掉了马。

normal.en: The preposition is usually for: people jostle for position or for attention.
normal.cn: 介词常用 for：人们争抢位置或争抢注意。

normal.en: The verb is regular: jostles, jostled, jostling.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：jostles、jostled、jostling。

normal.en: The passive be jostled by is very common on busy streets and trains.
normal.cn: 被动式「be jostled by」在繁忙街道和列车上十分常见。

normal.en: Compare shove: shove is one directed push, jostle is repeated bumping among many people.
normal.cn: 对比 shove：shove 是一次定向的推，jostle 是许多人之间反反复复的碰撞。

abstract.en: Picture a crush at the doors when a train arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象列车进站时车门前的拥堵冲撞。

abstract.en: Picture elbows and shopping bags colliding on a narrow street.
abstract.cn: 想象窄街上手肘和购物袋互相碰撞。

abstract.en: Picture brands crowding a shelf, each trying to stand in front of the next.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上各品牌挤作一堆，每个都想站到别人前面。

examples.en: Reporters jostled for a better view of the stage.
examples.cn: 记者们争抢着要占据看得更清楚的位置。

examples.en: She was jostled by the crowd outside the station.
examples.cn: 她在车站外被人群挤来挤去。

examples.en: Small shops jostle with big chains on the high street.
examples.cn: 商业街上小店与大连锁店相互挤占。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「较死捋」——在人群里较着劲、死死捋紧背包往前拱，一路推推撞撞，正是 jostle 的推挤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 iuxta（旁边）+ 撞击、比武之意 → 古法语 joster（聚集比武）→ 英语 joust（骑士对冲）→ jostle（反复推撞、争抢），核心义「并排相贴、互相挤撞」。

sensesIntro.en: Jostle moves from pushing in a crowd through forcing a way forward, then turns physical jostling into the struggle for market share and attention, and finally treats jostling as a noun and as pressure on ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: jostle 从人推人出发，经由推挤前行，再转为对份额与注意力的争夺，最后以名词形式指一次碰撞，并引申为对观点施压。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bodies pressed side by side, knocking against one another in a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群里身体并排相贴，彼此撞来撞去。

branches.en: The crowd press, one bump, and the elbow shove are the literal body senses.
branches.cn: 人群推挤、一记碰撞与用肘挤撞都是身体层面的本义。

branches.en: Pushing against others doubles as a way of getting through.
branches.cn: 推撞他人同时也是一种穿行的方式。

branches.en: Market share and attention are the prizes of a crowded scramble.
branches.cn: 市场份额与注意力是拥挤争夺中的战利品。

branches.en: Objects in a narrow space are shaken aside just like people.
branches.cn: 狭小空间里的物品也会像人一样被撞歪。

branches.en: Beliefs and roles can be pressed on as if they were bodies in a crowd.
branches.cn: 信念与角色也能被施压，仿佛人群中的身体。

intro.en: Jostle is a frequentative verb from joust, with jostling and jostler built on it.
intro.cn: jostle 是由 joust 派生的反复动词，并衍生出 jostling 与 jostler。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind it is iuxta, beside, fused into the Old French jousting verb joster.
latinIntro.cn: 其背后的拉丁语是 iuxta（旁边），并入古法语比武动词 joster。

items.example: Joster is the Old French source of joust.
items.exampleCN: joster 是 joust 的古法语来源。

items.example: Knights once jousted for honour.
items.exampleCN: 骑士们曾为荣誉比武。

items.example: The suffix -le makes joustle into a repeated action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -le 把动作变成反复进行的动作。

items.meaning: to bump and push in a crowd
items.example: Jostle keeps the repeated knock of the crowd.
items.exampleCN: jostle 保留了人群里反复的碰撞。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms jostling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 jostling。

items.example: Jostling filled the narrow market street.
items.exampleCN: 狭窄的市场街挤满了推推搡搡的人。

items.example: The suffix -er forms jostler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 jostler。

items.example: A jostler shoved past the queue.
items.exampleCN: 一个推推撞撞的人挤过了队伍。

items.example: The line jostles as the doors open.
items.exampleCN: 车门一开，队伍就推挤起来。

items.example: Jostled passengers reached for the hand rail.
items.exampleCN: 被挤来挤去的乘客纷纷去抓扶手。

definition_zh: 欢乐的；充满喜悦的；令人愉快的
definition_en: full of joy, or showing great and cheerful gladness
core_image: 阳光下的草坪上，一群人张开双臂又笑又跳
scene: 音乐节最后一晚，舞台下的人群跟着节拍一起挥手欢笑。On the last night of the music festival, the whole crowd was joyous.
sceneCN: 这里 joyous 是「欢乐的、洋溢着喜悦的」（第 1 个义项：充满喜悦并表现于外的）；句意：音乐节最后一晚，整个人群都沉浸在欢乐之中。

pos.zh: 欢乐的；喜悦的；令人愉快的

derivatives.zh: 由 joyous 加 -ly 构成，义为「欢快地」
由 joyous 加 -ness 构成，义为「欢乐的样子」
词根名词，义为「喜悦」
由 joy 加 -ful 构成，义为「快乐的」，与 joyous 义近
由前缀 en- 加 joy 构成，义为「享受」

senses.title: Full of visible joy
senses.definition: feeling and openly showing great happiness and gladness
senses.definitionCN: 感到并毫不掩饰地表现出极大的喜悦与高兴
senses.example: The new parents were a joyous pair at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 这对新晋父母在聚会上笑逐颜开，满是喜悦。
senses.why: The Latin base gaudium means joy, so the adjective names a person filled with it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 gaudium 意为「喜悦」，因此这个形容词指向充满喜悦的人或人群。

senses.title: Cheerful in appearance
senses.definition: having a bright, cheerful quality that other people can see or hear
senses.definitionCN: 带有明亮欢快的特质，旁人看得见或听得出来
senses.example: Her voice took on a joyous ring at the good news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个好消息，她的声音里透出欢快。
senses.why: The suffix -ous means full of, so joyous describes the quality that radiates from a face or voice.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 表示「充满……的」，所以 joyous 描述从脸上或声音里散发出来的特质。

senses.title: Glad or festive in tone
senses.definition: causing or expressing happiness, used of events, songs, and times
senses.definitionCN: 带来或表达快乐的，常用于场合、歌曲与时光
senses.example: It was a joyous day for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 那一天对全村来说都是喜庆欢乐的日子。
senses.why: From people the word spreads to the things they fill, so an occasion itself can be called joyous.
senses.whyCN: 从人的情绪扩展到他们所充满的事物，因此场合本身也能被称为「喜庆的」。

senses.title: Literary or formal register
senses.definition: a more elevated and formal way of saying happy, especially in writing
senses.definitionCN: happy 的更高雅、更正式的书面说法
senses.example: The poet writes of a bright morning after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人写到暴风雨之后那个明亮的早晨。
senses.why: Coming through Old French, joyous kept a literary tone while plain happy became the everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 经古法语传入后，joyous 保留了文学色彩，而平实的 happy 成了日常用词。

intro.en: Joyous comes from Latin gaudium, joy, through Old French joios, and shares its base with Middle English joy.
intro.cn: joyous 源自拉丁语 gaudium（喜悦），经古法语 joios 传入，与中古英语的 joy 同源。

items.en: Gaudium means joy, built on the verb gaudere, to rejoice.
items.cn: gaudium 意为喜悦，来自动词 gaudere（高兴、欢欣）。

items.en: Gaudiosus means full of joy, adding the suffix -osus, full of.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 gaudiosus 意为「充满喜悦的」，加的是后缀 -osus（满……的）。

items.en: Joios carries the word into French as glad or joyful.
items.cn: 古法语 joios 把这个词带入法语，义为「高兴的、喜悦的」。

items.en: The spelling joyos first appears in Middle English verse.
items.cn: 拼写 joyos 首次出现在中古英语诗歌中。

items.en: The modern form joyous settles into formal and literary style.
items.cn: 现代英语中 joyous 定型，多用于正式或文学语体。

note.en: Joyous belongs to the joy family of words and sits between everyday happy and stronger exultant.
note.cn: joyous 属于 joy 这一词族，语义介于日常的 happy 与更强的 exultant 之间。

entries.definition: very happy and full of joy, formed with -ful
entries.definitionCN: 义为「非常快乐的」，用 -ful 构成，与 joyous 同族近义

entries.definition: the noun of gladness from which the adjective is built
entries.definitionCN: 表示喜悦的名词，是构成该形容词的基础词

entries.definition: cheerful and friendly
entries.definitionCN: 义为「快活友善的」，只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自罗马主神之名）

entries.definition: feeling or showing pleasure
pleased and happy about something
bright and pleasant in manner

normalIntro.en: Joyous is joy plus -ous, so it simply means full of joy and showing it.
normalIntro.cn: joyous 就是 joy 加 -ous，意思很直接：充满喜悦并表现出来。

normal.en: A joyous occasion is a happy and festive event.
normal.cn: a joyous occasion 指欢乐而喜庆的场合。

normal.en: Joyous and joyful both come from joy; joyous is more literary.
normal.cn: joyous 与 joyful 都来自 joy，其中 joyous 更偏文学书面。

normal.en: Joyously means in a happy, delighted way.
normal.cn: joyously 意为欢快地、兴高采烈地。

normal.en: Joyousness is the state of being full of joy.
normal.cn: joyousness 指充满喜悦的状态。

normal.en: Do not confuse joyous with jovial, which comes from the god Jupiter.
normal.cn: 不要把 joyous 与 jovial 混淆，后者来自神的名字 Jupiter。

abstract.en: Picture a wedding crowd throwing rice and laughing in the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象婚礼上人群在阳光下撒米大笑。

abstract.en: Hear a choir singing a bright, rising melody at the end of the night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里最后，合唱队唱起明亮上扬的旋律。

abstract.en: See a child jumping off a swing with arms wide open.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子从秋千上跳下来，双臂张开。

examples.en: The whole street was joyous after the team won the cup.
examples.cn: 球队夺冠后，整条街都欢腾起来。

examples.en: The choir sang joyously as the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 宾客到来时，合唱团欢快地唱着歌。

examples.en: Their reunion was full of tears and laughter.
examples.cn: 他们的重聚充满着泪水与欢笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乔一额」——乔迁之喜，大家都额手称庆，一片欢乐；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gaudium（喜悦）→ gaudiosus（充满喜悦的）→ 古法语 joios → 中古英语 joyos → 现代英语 joyous，核心义「充满喜悦」。

sensesIntro.en: Joyous moves from a person full of joy, to the cheerful quality that shows, to festive occasions, and finally to a literary register.
sensesIntro.cn: joyous 从充满喜悦的人，扩展到外显的欢快特质，再到喜庆场合，最后落为一种文学语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sunlit crowd laughing with arms open.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光下张开双臂欢笑的人群。

branches.en: A person or group openly full of joy.
branches.cn: 指公开充满喜悦的人或人群。

branches.en: The cheerful quality that shows in face or voice.
branches.cn: 显露在表情或声音里的欢快特质。

branches.en: Happy and festive events, songs, and days.
branches.cn: 令人愉快、喜庆的场合、歌曲与日子。

branches.en: The elevated written use of the word.
branches.cn: 这个词高雅的书面用法。

branches.en: A cheerful voice and a festive day both radiate joy.
branches.cn: 欢快的声音与喜庆的日子都在散发喜悦。

intro.en: Joyous builds on the noun joy with the adjective suffix -ous, and shares ground with joyful and enjoy.
intro.cn: joyous 由名词 joy 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，与 joyful、enjoy 共享同一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gaudium, joy, and its adjective gaudiosus, full of joy, sit behind the French form that gave English the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gaudium（喜悦）及其形容词 gaudiosus（充满喜悦的），是法语形式之前的上源。

items.example: Joy is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: joy 是这一词族的基础名词。

items.meaning: having or full of a quality
items.meaningCN: 具有或充满某种性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ous forms joyous from joy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 由 joy 构成 joyous。

items.example: Joyous describes a person or scene of joy.
items.exampleCN: joyous 形容充满喜悦的人或场景。

items.example: The adverb -ly marks manner.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 表示方式。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms joyousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 joyousness。

items.example: Joyful uses -ful instead of -ous.
items.exampleCN: joyful 用 -ful 而非 -ous 构成。

items.example: The prefix en- forms enjoy.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 构成 enjoy。

items.example: Enjoy keeps the joy inside the verb.
items.exampleCN: enjoy 把 joy 藏在动词里。

items.example: Enjoyment comes from enjoy plus -ment.
items.exampleCN: enjoyment 由 enjoy 加 -ment 构成。

items.example: The suffix -less gives the opposite joyless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 给出反义的 joyless。

definition_zh: 欢欣鼓舞的；喜气洋洋的；欢呼雀跃的
definition_en: feeling and showing great happiness, especially because of a success
core_image: 夺冠那一刻，看台上的人群跳起来挥拳高呼
scene: 冠军揭晓的一刻，球迷们从座位上跳起来互相拥抱。Fans jumped from their seats and hugged each other, jubilant at the news.
sceneCN: 这里 jubilant 是「欢欣鼓舞的、喜气洋洋的」（第 1 个义项：因喜讯或成功而狂喜）；句意：球迷们从座位上跳起来互相拥抱，为这个消息而欢欣鼓舞。

pos.zh: 欢欣鼓舞的；喜气洋洋的

derivatives.zh: 由 jubilant 加 -ly 构成，义为「欢欣鼓舞地」
由拉丁语词根 jubil- 加 -ation 构成，义为「欢腾；欢庆」
由 jubilant 加 -ance 构成，义为「欢欣」
同源于希伯来语，义为「周年庆典；大赦年」

senses.title: Triumphantly happy
senses.definition: full of great joy and triumph, especially after a success or a piece of good news
senses.definitionCN: 在成功或得到好消息后充满极大喜悦与胜利感的
senses.example: The team was jubilant after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后，球队欢欣鼓舞。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to shout for joy, so the core sense is joy loud enough to be heard.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「为喜悦而呼喊」，所以核心含义是响亮到能被人听见的喜悦。

senses.title: Exulting over a win
senses.definition: openly exulting because of victory or advantage over others
senses.definitionCN: 因胜利或胜过他人而公开地兴高采烈
senses.example: Jubilant voters filled the square after the result.
senses.exampleCN: 结果公布后，喜气洋洋的选民挤满了广场。
senses.why: Because the word attaches to shouting, it suits the winners who make the loudest noise.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词与「呼喊」相连，它特别适合形容发出最大声响的胜利者。

senses.title: Cheerful, high spirits
senses.definition: in very high spirits, bubbling with excitement even without a clear cause
senses.definitionCN: 情绪非常高昂，即使没有明显缘由也兴奋洋溢
senses.example: The children were jubilant on the last day of term.
senses.exampleCN: 学期最后一天，孩子们兴高采烈。
senses.why: The sense widens from victory to any overflow of high spirits.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「获胜」扩展到任何高涨情绪的洋溢。

senses.title: Congratulatory in tone
senses.definition: describing words, songs, or writing that celebrate someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 形容庆祝某人或某事的言辞、歌曲或文字
senses.example: The paper ran a jubilant headline about the rescue.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸为这次营救刊出了充满欢呼口吻的标题。
senses.why: From describing people, the adjective extends to the messages those people shout or print.
senses.whyCN: 从形容人，扩展到形容这些人所喊出或印出的祝贺之辞。

intro.en: Jubilant comes from the Latin verb iubilare, to shout for joy, which passes through the noun jubilans into the English adjective.
intro.cn: jubilant 源自拉丁语动词 iubilare（为喜悦而呼喊），经名词 jubilans 变成英语形容词。

items.en: Yovel names a ram or a ram horn blown in celebration.
items.cn: 希伯来语 yovel 指公羊或节庆时吹的羊角号。

items.en: Iubilare means to shout or call out, also used of farmers calling out.
items.cn: 拉丁语 iubilare 意为呼喊、出声，也用于形容农人呼唤。

items.en: In Christian Latin the verb grows to mean to shout for joy.
items.cn: 在基督教拉丁语中，这个动词发展为「为喜悦而欢呼」。

items.en: Jubilant settles as the present participle from Latin jubilans.
items.cn: 古法语按拉丁语 jubilans 的现在分词形式确立为 jubilant。

items.en: English takes the adjective jubilant in Early Modern use and pairs it with jubilee.
items.cn: 英语在早期现代阶段采用形容词 jubilant，并把它与 jubilee 相配。

note.en: Jubilant is the loud, public face of joy, and it shares a lineage with jubilee and jubilation.
note.cn: jubilant 是喜悦那副响亮、公开的面孔，并与 jubilee、jubilation 同源。

entries.definition: a feeling of great joy and celebration
entries.definitionCN: 指欢腾、欢庆的情绪，是与 jubilant 同根的抽象名词

entries.definition: a special anniversary or celebration
entries.definitionCN: 指周年纪念或隆重庆典，词源上与 jubilant 相通

entries.definition: in a joyful, exulting manner
entries.definitionCN: 义为「欢欣地」，是 jubilant 派生的副词

entries.definition: showing great joy after a triumph
entries.definitionCN: 指胜利之后欢欣得意的

entries.definition: winning or showing victory
entries.definitionCN: 指获胜的或表现出胜利的

entries.definition: extremely happy and excited

normalIntro.en: Jubilant keeps the shout of joy inside it, so it always sounds loud and public.
normalIntro.cn: jubilant 里藏着「欢呼」的回声，所以它总带着响亮、公开的色彩。

normal.en: A jubilant crowd is one that has something to cheer about.
normal.cn: a jubilant crowd 一定是遇上值得欢呼之事的群体。

normal.en: The noun jubilation names the cheering itself.
normal.cn: 名词 jubilation 指的就是那阵欢呼。

normal.en: Jubilantly adds the -ly adverb ending.
normal.cn: jubilantly 就是加上 -ly 副词词尾。

normal.en: Jubilant and jubilee come from the same celebration word.
normal.cn: jubilant 与 jubilee 来自同一个表示庆祝的词源。

normal.en: Use jubilant for winners and crowds, not for quiet private happiness.
normal.cn: jubilant 用于胜者与人群，不形容安静的私人喜悦。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium erupting as the winning goal goes in.
abstract.cn: 想象制胜球入网、球场瞬间爆发的画面。

abstract.en: Hear ten thousand people shouting one name at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一万人同时高喊同一个名字。

abstract.en: See flags going up like a flock of birds taking off.
abstract.cn: 想象旗帜一起升起，像一群鸟同时起飞。

examples.en: The jubilant winners lifted the trophy high.
examples.cn: 欢欣雀跃的获胜者把奖杯高高举起。

examples.en: Grapes were picked in a jubilant, noisy harvest.
examples.cn: 葡萄在欢腾喧闹的收成中采摘。

examples.en: She was jubilant when the letter of acceptance arrived.
examples.cn: 录取信到手时，她欢欣鼓舞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朱必乐」——朱红色的庆典上大家必定快乐地欢呼；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 iubilare（呼喊、为喜悦而欢呼）→ 后期拉丁语 jubilans → 古法语 jubilant → 英语 jubilant；更早或与希伯来语 yovel（公羊、羊角号）有关，词源仍有讨论。核心义「为喜悦而高声欢呼」。

sensesIntro.en: Jubilant starts as joy loud enough to shout, tightens onto victory, loosens into general high spirits, and finally describes congratulatory words.
sensesIntro.cn: jubilant 从响亮的喜悦出发，收窄到胜利者的欢呼，再放宽为一般的高昂情绪，最后形容祝贺性的言辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd leaping up with fists in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群挥舞拳头跳起来。

branches.en: Triumphant, excited happiness after success.
branches.cn: 成功之后的狂喜与兴奋。

branches.en: The exultation of those who have won.
branches.cn: 获胜者公开表现出的得意欢欣。

branches.en: Overflowing high spirits with no clear cause.
branches.cn: 没有明显缘由的情绪高涨。

branches.en: Words and headlines that celebrate something.
branches.cn: 庆祝某事所用的言辞与标题。

branches.en: Winners experience the loudest, most visible joy.
branches.cn: 胜者经历的是最响亮、最显眼的喜悦。

intro.en: Jubilant is a borrowed Latin participle in -ant, and the English family grows with -ly, -ance, and the noun jubilation.
intro.cn: jubilant 是借自拉丁语的 -ant 分词形式，英语词族借 -ly、-ance 与名词 jubilation 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin iubilare, to shout for joy, gives the participle jubilans and the noun jubilatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iubilare（为喜悦而呼喊）给出分词 jubilans 与名词 jubilatio。

items.example: The root jubil- carries the cry of joy.
items.exampleCN: 词根 jubil- 承载着欢呼的声音。

items.meaningCN: 具有或表现某种性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant turns the verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 把动词变为形容词。

items.example: Jubilant keeps the loud joy of the root.
items.exampleCN: jubilant 保留了词根里响亮的喜悦。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms jubilantly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 jubilantly。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms jubilation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 jubilation。

items.example: Jubilation is the cheering itself.
items.exampleCN: jubilation 指欢呼本身。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ance forms jubilance.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 构成 jubilance。

items.example: Jubilance is a rare noun of the state.
items.exampleCN: jubilance 是较罕见的表示状态的同族名词。

items.example: Jubilee shares the celebration thread.
items.exampleCN: jubilee 共享「庆典」这条线索。

definition_zh: 明智的；审慎的；有见地的
definition_en: showing good sense and careful judgement, especially about practical matters
core_image: 法官在案卷前戴上眼镜，逐条比对证据后才落笔
scene: 预算有限，经理反复权衡各项开支后才决定先保哪一块。The manager made a judicious choice among the limited options.
sceneCN: 这里 judicious 是「明智的、审慎的」（第 1 个义项：经仔细判断后作出的选择）；句意：经理在有限的选择中做出了明智的抉择。

pos.zh: 明智的；审慎的；有判断力的

derivatives.zh: 由 judicious 加 -ly 构成，义为「明智地；审慎地」
由 judicious 加 -ness 构成，义为「审慎；明智」
与 judicious 同源于「判断」，义为「判断；裁决」
同源基础词，义为「法官；判断」

senses.title: Showing good judgement
senses.definition: decided or done with careful thought and sound practical sense
senses.definitionCN: 经过认真思考、具有良好实际判断力的
senses.example: The council took a judicious view of the costs.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会对费用问题作了明智的考量。
senses.why: The Latin root iudex means one who judges, so the adjective means showing the quality of a good judge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 iudex 意为「审判者」，因此这个形容词表示具备好法官那样的素质。

senses.title: Prudent in management
senses.titleCN: 节省得当的；用得恰到好处的
senses.definition: careful and economical in the way resources are used
senses.definitionCN: 在使用资源时谨慎、节约且恰到好处
senses.example: Judicious use of water kept the garden alive.
senses.exampleCN: 把水用得恰到好处，让花园得以存活。
senses.why: Good judgement in practical matters usually shows up as careful spending and use.
senses.whyCN: 在实务上的好判断，通常就表现为谨慎地花费和使用。

senses.title: Balanced and well-considered
senses.definition: balanced, not extreme, after weighing several factors
senses.definitionCN: 权衡多个因素之后达到的平衡、不走极端的
senses.example: The essay strikes a judicious balance between praise and doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在褒扬与质疑之间取得了恰当的平衡。
senses.why: A judge hears both sides, so the word also suggests weighting evidence before deciding.
senses.whyCN: 法官要兼听双方，所以这个词也暗含「先权衡证据再作决定」。

senses.title: Formal praise of advisers
senses.definition: used in formal writing to praise a person or policy as sound and wise
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中赞许某个人或政策稳妥、有远见
senses.example: Her judicious advice saved the project from collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 她有见地的建议使项目免于崩溃。
senses.why: The Latin ending -ous gives a formal adjective, so the word reads as measured praise in written English.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词尾 -ous 使它成为正式形容词，在书面英语中读来像有分寸的褒奖。

intro.en: Judicious comes from French judicieux, from Latin iudicium, judgement, built on iudex, a judge.
intro.cn: judicious 来自法语 judicieux，源自拉丁语 iudicium（判断），后者由 iudex（审判者）构成。

items.en: Ius means law or right and dico means to say, giving iudex, one who declares the law.
items.cn: ius 意为法或权利，dico 意为说出，合为 iudex，即宣告法律之人。

items.en: Iudicium means a judgement or a trial.
items.cn: iudicium 意为判断、审判。

items.en: Judicieux takes shape as the French adjective of good judgement.
items.cn: 法语形容词 judicieux 形成，表示「有判断力的」。

items.en: Judicious enters English in the sixteenth century alongside judicial.
items.cn: judicious 于十六世纪进入英语，与 judicial 一同出现。

items.en: The word settles into formal praise of prudent decisions and use.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，它定型为对审慎决策与用度的正式褒扬。

note.en: Judicious shares the judge family of words and suggests careful judgement rather than mere cleverness.
note.cn: judicious 与 judge 一族的词同源，强调仔细判断，而不是单纯的聪明。

entries.definition: relating to courts and judges
entries.definitionCN: 指与法庭、法官有关的，与 judicious 同根但意义不同

entries.definition: the court system as a whole
a person who decides cases or forms an opinion
entries.definitionCN: 指审判者，也指作出评判的人

entries.definition: careful about the future and risks
entries.definitionCN: 指为将来和风险着想而谨慎的

entries.definition: showing good practical sense
entries.definitionCN: 指具有良好实际判断力的

entries.definition: careful not to attract attention or say too much
entries.definitionCN: 指谨慎、不张扬、不多言的

normalIntro.en: Judicious is judge plus -icious, so it means thinking like a careful judge before acting.
normalIntro.cn: judicious 就是 judge 加 -icious，意思是像细心的法官那样先想清楚再行动。

normal.en: A judicious choice is one a careful judge would approve.
normal.cn: judicious choice 是连细心的法官都会认可的选择。

normal.en: Judiciously fits the -ly adverb slot.
normal.cn: judiciously 是加 -ly 的副词形式。

normal.en: Keep judicial for courts and judicious for good sense.
normal.cn: judicial 留给法庭，judicious 留给明智。

normal.en: The related noun judgment is what judiciousness shows.
normal.cn: 同族名词 judgment 正是 judiciousness 所体现的东西。

normal.en: In exams, judicious use of time beats rushing.
normal.cn: 考试中，明智地使用时间胜过一味赶时间。

abstract.en: Picture a judge weighing each page of evidence before signing.
abstract.cn: 想象法官签字前逐页掂量证据。

abstract.en: Imagine pouring water from a small cup, drop by drop.
abstract.cn: 想象用小杯一滴一滴地倒水。

abstract.en: See a scale that stays level because weights were chosen well.
abstract.cn: 想象一台因砝码选得恰到好处而保持水平的天平。

examples.en: She made a judicious use of the limited budget.
examples.cn: 她对有限的预算作了明智的使用。

examples.en: The doctor was judicious in prescribing antibiotics.
examples.cn: 这位医生开抗生素时非常审慎。

examples.en: A judicious mix of work and rest keeps people healthy.
examples.cn: 劳逸恰当结合使人保持健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「居地势」——站高一层看局势，往往更能作出明智的判断；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 iudex（审判者）= ius（法、权利）+ dicere（说）→ iudicium（判断）→ 古法语 judicieux → 英语 judicious，核心义「善于判断」。

sensesIntro.en: Judicious runs from the general sense of good judgement, to careful use of resources, to a balanced view, and finally to formal praise.
sensesIntro.cn: judicious 从一般的「判断力好」，到谨慎使用资源，到持平的判断，最后落到正式的褒扬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a judge weighing the evidence before signing.
core.cn: 核心意象：法官签字前权衡证据。

branches.en: Decisions made with sound practical sense.
branches.cn: 凭良好实务判断作出的决定。

branches.en: Economical, well-aimed use of resources.
branches.cn: 对资源节约而准确的运用。

branches.en: A balanced, non-extreme position.
branches.cn: 平衡、不走极端的立场。

branches.en: Formal written praise for people and policies.
branches.cn: 对人与政策的正式书面褒扬。

branches.en: Good judgement means weighing both sides before deciding.
branches.cn: 好判断意味着决定前兼顾双方。

intro.en: Judicious is built on the judge root with the adjective suffix -ous, and the English family grows with -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: judicious 由 judge 词根加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，英语词族借 -ly 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius, law, and dicere, to say, combine in iudex, a judge, and iudicium, a judgement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius（法）与 dicere（说）合成 iudex（审判者）与 iudicium（判断）。

items.meaning: to judge, to pass a sentence
items.example: The root judic- carries the act of judging.
items.exampleCN: 词根 judic- 承载「判断」这一动作。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms judicious from it.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 由它构成 judicious。

items.example: Judicious praises careful judgement.
items.exampleCN: judicious 褒扬的是仔细的判断。

items.example: Judge is the plain everyday base.
items.exampleCN: judge 是日常的基础词。

items.example: Judgment names the result of judging.
items.exampleCN: judgment 指判断的结果。

items.example: Judicial belongs to the courtroom.
items.exampleCN: judicial 属于法庭语境。

items.example: Judiciary names the whole court system.
items.exampleCN: judiciary 指整套法院系统。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms judiciously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 judiciously。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms judiciousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 judiciousness。

definition_zh: 使混杂；弄乱；混乱的一堆；杂乱无章
definition_en: to mix things together in a disorderly way, or a confused untidy mixture
core_image: 抽屉里的耳机线、钥匙和糖纸缠成一团，越扒拉越乱
scene: 搬家当天屋里最乱。By the evening every room was filled with a jumble of boxes and old clothes.
sceneCN: 这里 jumble 是「杂乱的一堆」（第 3 个义项：东西混在一起形成的一团）；句意：到了晚上，每个房间都堆满了箱子和旧衣服混成一团的杂物。

derivatives.zh: 动词 jumble 加过去分词词尾构成，义为「混乱的；杂乱的」
基础词加形容词词尾 -y 构成，义为「杂乱无章的」（口语）

senses.title: To mix things up in disorder
senses.definition: to put things together in a careless orderless way
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的东西乱堆乱放，不留次序
senses.example: She jumbled all the photos into one cardboard box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把所有照片胡乱塞进一个纸箱里。
senses.why: The core image is several things thrown into one heap so that no order is left.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把几样东西丢进同一堆里，原先的次序全部消失，所以动词义就是「使混杂、弄乱」。

senses.title: To confuse or scramble ideas
senses.definition: to mix up information or ideas so that they no longer make sense
senses.definitionCN: 把信息或想法打乱，使其失去条理
senses.example: The long journey had jumbled his sense of time.
senses.exampleCN: 长途旅行把他的时间感都搅乱了。
senses.why: When the things thrown together are facts or thoughts, the physical heap turns into mental confusion.
senses.whyCN: 被扔在一起的若是事实或想法，具体的乱堆就转成头脑里的混乱，所以有了「搅乱（思路）」的义项。

senses.title: A confused mixture
senses.definition: an untidy collection of different things mixed together
senses.definitionCN: 不同东西混在一起形成的一团杂乱物
senses.example: The teacher waded through a jumble of old papers and magazines.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在旧报纸和杂志混成一团的东西里翻找。
senses.why: The verb names the act of heaping things up, and the noun names the heap itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词指「堆起来」这个动作，名词就指堆出来的那一摊，所以 jumble 也可以直接指「杂乱的一堆」。

senses.title: An untidy heap of low-value goods
senses.definition: a heap of cheap or used goods sold for charity, chiefly in British use
senses.definitionCN: 为慈善出售的一堆旧货或廉价物品，多见于英式英语
senses.example: We found a jumble of old toys at the village fair.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在村里的义卖会上看到一堆旧玩具。
senses.why: British shops turned the untidy heap into a charity stall, so the noun came to name the pile of donated goods.
senses.whyCN: 英式用法把这种乱堆搬到慈善摊位上，于是 jumble 又用来指义卖现场那堆捐来的旧杂货。

intro.en: Jumble is generally traced to a word meaning to mix or confuse, with no secure Latin or Greek ancestor; its exact source is uncertain.
intro.cn: jumble 一般认为可追溯到表示「混合、弄混」的词语，没有可靠的拉丁或希腊语祖先，确切来源存疑。

items.en: The word first appears in English as a verb for mixing things in confusion, with no certain earlier source.
items.cn: 这个词最早在英语中作动词，表示把东西胡乱混在一起，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Jumble is recorded in the sixteenth century meaning to mix up in disorder.
items.cn: jumble 在十六世纪有记录，意为胡乱混合、搅乱。

items.en: The noun for a confused heap appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 表示「混乱的一堆」的名词义在十七世纪出现。

items.en: British charity stalls give the jumble sale its name from the miscellany of donated goods.
items.cn: 英国慈善摊位因为捐来的杂货五花八门，便把这种摊子称为 jumble sale。

items.en: In modern English the word keeps both the act of mixing and the resulting heap.
items.cn: 在现代英语里，这个词同时保留「混合的动作」与「混合后的那堆东西」两个意思。

note.en: Jumble is the jostling heap; its look-alikes share the sound and letters, while its near meanings name other kinds of disorder.
note.cn: jumble 强调的是互相挤压的乱堆；形近组与它共享读音和字母，近义组则列出别的「混乱」说法。

entries.definition: a continuous deep sound, as of distant thunder
entries.definitionCN: 持续低沉的响声，如远处的雷声；只是拼写结尾相同，词源不同

entries.definition: to fall suddenly and heavily
entries.definitionCN: 跌倒；翻滚落下；只是拼写结尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to move or act clumsily
entries.definitionCN: 笨手笨脚地做事；只是拼写结尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to put different things together
entries.definitionCN: 把不同的东西放在一起；常是自愿有序的混合

entries.definition: to make something unclear or muddled
an untidy collection of things filling a space

normalIntro.en: These hooks work through the sound of the word, the fixed phrase jumble sale and the everyday verb picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子借助这个词的读音、固定说法 jumble sale 以及日常的动词画面。

normal.en: The j- sound is quick and bumpy, like things dropping onto a heap.
normal.cn: 开头的 j 音短促起伏，像东西一件件丢到堆上。

normal.en: Jumble up is the everyday verb for messing a drawer or a list.
normal.cn: jumble up 就是日常说「把抽屉或清单弄乱」的动词。

normal.en: A jumble sale is a British charity stall full of mismatched odds and ends.
normal.cn: jumble sale 是英国慈善摊，里面全是配不上对的杂物。

normal.en: A jumble of boxes is the fixed way to say a heap of unrelated containers.
normal.cn: a jumble of boxes 是固定说法，指一堆互不相干的箱子。

normal.en: Compare mix: mix can be orderly, but jumble always leaves things in a mess.
normal.cn: 对比 mix：mix 可以是有序的混合，jumble 却总留下乱糟糟的局面。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer where earphones, keys and receipts have wrapped into one knot.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里耳机线、钥匙和收据缠成一个结。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of jumbled photos where holidays and birthdays no longer sit in order.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上照片全乱了，假期和生日的顺序都分不清。

abstract.en: Picture a table covered with a jumble of unmatched cups and papers.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面上摊着一堆配不成套的杯子和纸张。

examples.en: The children jumbled bricks, cars and dolls into one big bowl.
examples.cn: 孩子们把积木、小汽车和洋娃娃全混进一个大盆里。

examples.en: Her notes were a jumble of names, dates and half finished plans.
examples.cn: 她的笔记是一堆姓名、日期和半成品计划混杂在一起的东西。

examples.en: He jumbled the two files by mistake.
examples.cn: 他一不小心把两份文件弄混了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎姆波」——听起来像一堆东西被挤到一起的闷响；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为与表示「混合、搅乱」的古老动词相连，也与 tumble、rumble 一类声音起伏的构词相呼应，但拉丁或希腊对应词并未确认。

sensesIntro.en: Jumble moves from the act of heaping things up, to confusing ideas, to the heap itself and finally to the British charity pile.
sensesIntro.cn: jumble 先从「把东西乱堆」的动作出发，再到「搅乱思路」，再到堆出来的那一摊，最后落到英国的旧货义卖堆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot of earphones, keys and receipts in one drawer.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里耳机线、钥匙和收据缠成一团。

branches.en: The physical act has no order.
branches.cn: 具体的乱放动作，毫无次序。

branches.en: The heap grows inside the mind.
branches.cn: 乱堆钻进头脑里，变成思路混乱。

branches.en: The heap is named as a thing.
branches.cn: 乱堆被当成一样东西来称呼。

branches.en: Both are heaps of unrelated items.
branches.cn: 两者都是一堆互不相配的物件。

branches.en: Jumbling facts muddles your thinking.
branches.cn: 把事实混在一起，思路必然乱掉。

intro.en: Jumble is built with the core jum- and the common English ending -ble, shared with rumble, tumble and bumble; the ending is not a Latin suffix.
intro.cn: jumble 由词干 jum- 加上常见的英语词尾 -ble 构成，与 rumble、tumble、bumble 共用这个结尾；这个结尾不是拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin source for jumble, so the word is best learned from its English endings and phrases.
latinIntro.cn: jumble 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，所以最好从它的英语词尾和固定搭配入手记忆。

items.example: Jum- carries the sense of a rough heap.
items.exampleCN: jum- 带着一团乱堆的感觉。

items.meaningCN: 表示声音或动作的词尾
items.example: The ending -ble also ends rumble and tumble.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ble 也出现在 rumble 与 tumble 里。

items.example: To jumble is to toss together.
items.exampleCN: jumble 就是把东西乱丢在一起。

items.example: Jumbled notes are hard to follow.
items.exampleCN: 混乱的笔记很难读懂。

items.example: The casual word jumbly describes a messy shelf.
items.exampleCN: 口语词 jumbly 形容乱糟糟的架子。

items.example: Do not jumble up the cards.
items.exampleCN: 别把卡片弄乱了。

items.example: The waiter jumbled the dishes together.
items.exampleCN: 服务员把盘子胡乱叠在一起。

items.meaning: a charity sale of used goods
items.example: A jumble sale raised money for the school.
items.exampleCN: 一场旧物义卖为学校筹了款。

items.example: A jumble of coats lay on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 地板上堆着一堆外套。
